content: On April 23, a Russian SU-27 fighter displayed a show of aggression towards a US RC-135U aircraft during a routine mission over the Sea of Okhotsk, reportedly employing threatening maneuvers and exposing air-to-air missiles. This incident occurred amidst ongoing tension between the US and Russia over Russia's involvement in Ukraine, with US President Barack Obama condemning Russian "aggression" in Ukraine in a speech earlier in the month.

The Prince of Wales, Charles, and his wife Camilla are embarking on a 12-day tour of Australia and New Zealand, marking the 15th time Charles visits Australia, and they will celebrate Charles' 67th birthday with a barbecue in Western Australia.

A 70-year-old woman was attacked in Sneem, County Kerry, on 20 September, while a man was detained by police on Saturday morning in Killarney, who is being questioned at the local Garda (police) station.

The Medical Practitioners Tribunal decided to erase Hugh McGoldrick's name from the medical register after his false conduct in drug trials on sleep disorder patients, as no appeal was filed before the 28-day deadline passed.
A 21-year-old male is under police investigation after a body was found in a wooded area in Dorking, Surrey, and Surrey Police is waiting for the results of a post-mortem examination.

A man identified as Josh Hanson was stabbed and died at the RE bar in Eastcote, Hillingdon. Over 40 people were reportedly at the bar at the time of the attack, and Scotland Yard urges anyone who was there or in the area around 01:00 Sunday to contact them with potential information, as no arrests have been made yet.

A potential new ferry service between Sandown and Southsea is suggested to increase tourism, with tentative plans for operational days on Tuesdays and Thursdays in July and August, and discussions underway between the Isle of Wight Council and Hovertravel to finalize details and secure necessary permissions.

On Sunday at roughly 02:00 BST, a 30-year-old man was viciously attacked by up to eight individuals in the Heights area, and while one suspect was arrested, he has since been released on bail as police continue to investigate and have appealed for information regarding the assault.

In the last two days, the death toll in flood-stricken areas of India, particularly Assam, has doubled as officials discovered over 100 bodies upon receding waters; the monsoon rains have affected 450,000 people in the state, with millions across at least 20 states being impacted nationwide, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi has pledged a visit to Assam to seek a permanent solution for the annual flooding in the region.

The Premier League's 25th anniversary season opens on Friday 11 August, with Arsenal hosting Leicester City, and Sky Sports will broadcast 10 Friday night matches as part of their multi-million pound deal. However, a significant third of Premier League football fans admit to regularly watching matches live online via unofficial streams.

Cristian Montano, a former Oldham Athletic midfielder with 48 appearances and 4 goals, was dismissed from the club following a thorough investigation into spot-fixing and was arrested by the National Crime Agency, with the club statement emphasizing that they take such matters seriously and acted swiftly.

A man, Rick Edwards, was sentenced to a suspended jail term and supervision order for setting a small piece of wallpaper on fire at a former Pontins resort in Brixham, which led to a extensive blaze that destroyed the 42-acre site and increased the final cost of demolition due to the damage caused and asbestos removal difficulties.

Footballer Chris Wilson, aged 30, re-joined Nottingham Forest from Celtic for £2.5m in 2013, making 51 appearances over four seasons before being released in May 2019, with a history also at Preston North End and Notts County.

In the second ODI of the five-match series in Colombo, Australia's left-arm seamer-Faulkner finished with 3 wickets (Kusal Perera, Angelo Mathews, Thisara Perera) to restrict Sri Lanka to 288. Australia, in response, were bowled out for 206, with Amila Aponso taking 4 wickets (4-18), including besting Wade's 76. This victory by 82 runs for Sri Lanka levels the series at 1-1. Additionally, Faulkner and Aponso are the latest in a line of Australian bowlers who have taken ODI hat-tricks, which includes Bruce Reid, Anthony Stuart, Brett Lee, Clint McKay, and Dan Christian.

Vadim Cobilas, a Sale Sharks player for the past decade, has decided to pursue a new opportunity in France's Top 14, and talks for contract extensions with David Seymour, Will Addison, and Mark Jennings are underway, while Chris Cusiter and Tommy Taylor's futures remain uncertain.

India, led by Shikhar Dhawan and Virat Kohli's centuries, appeared to be on course for their highest successful run-chase in Australia. However, a dramatic collapse saw India lose 9 wickets for just 46 runs, with Kane Richardson taking 5-68, leaving Australia in a position to secure a series whitewash in Sydney.

The Hammersmith and City Line and parts of the Circle Line have been temporarily suspended due to debris fears resulting from a fire in a 24-story block, at the request of the London Fire Brigade, with the aim of securing the area and potentially saving more lives as over 58 fatalities have been presumed so far.
Scottish footballer Jamie Hamill, previously of Hearts, has returned to his former club Kilmarnock after signing a three-year contract, set to make his 150th appearance there upon his second debut.
Ross Morgan, an Ipswich fan, celebrated Paul Anderson's goal by punching the ceiling in excitement, causing a hole, but Anderson, the goal-scorer, offered to cover the repair costs as a gesture.

Retailers in Wales are now required to keep tobacco products out of public view, a move aimed at reducing the appeal of smoking and improving public health, with violators facing fines and imprisonment.

Lucas, a 20-year-old footballer, is set to join Bristol Rovers' League Two team for a third time this season, having scored three goals in ten appearances for a National League side, and his manager suggests he could add goals and versatility to their forward line.

Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire is undergoing restoration, including waterproofing and rebuilding of the chimney stack, with night-time work on the platform canopy aimed at minimizing disruptions, as noted by both Network Rail and train operator Northern, who acknowledge the station's historical beauty.

Former NFL player Lawrence Phillips, a 1990s star at the University of Nebraska, is believed to have committed suicide early on Wednesday, following legal troubles that included assault convictions and a prison term for vehicular manslaughter, according to officials and reports.

The article discusses a proposed extension of Belfast's bus lane hours for the BRT plan, from the current 07:30 to 09:30 and 15:30 to 18:30, to 07:00 to 19:00, with a view to improving consistency and reducing confusion. Two rounds of consultation are planned, considering flexible options like designated loading and unloading windows. The project aims for a high frequency of buses and vehicles, with a focus on ensuring effective implementation.

Lionel Messi scored the winning goal for Barcelona in their La Liga game against Atletico Madrid, extending his record as the competition's all-time top scorer, after missing training to be with his newborn son. This occurred on the same day that Real Madrid's Cristiano Ronaldo broke his club's record for the most league goals.

Over 70 individuals, including players and directors from Italian third and fourth division clubs, are under investigation for "conspiracy to commit sporting fraud," with links to the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate, and police are investigating suspicious results in dozens of matches.

Spiderlings of a hybrid species between the Dolomedes plantarius found in Sussex and Suffolk were released in suitable dykes at Castle Marshes, with the aim that the increased genetic variability in the new population will help it adapt to its environment and climate change, funded by the BBC Wildlife Fund.

In August 1947, India and Pakistan gained independence from British rule (Partition), resulting in mass refugee movements and personal hardships, as depicted in a woman's account of her family's experience during this significant historical event.

Iva Barr, a veteran marathon runner with 30 years of experience, participated in her 20th marathon despite not completing the full route. She took the Underground to Westminster and walked the last part to The Mall, expressing joy and gratitude for the supportive crowd, especially the young people, and holding no regrets for her attempt.

In China's top cities, some young couples resort to staging fake divorces to purchase additional homes, amidst an increasingly unaffordable property market where escalating prices outpace low wages despite the central bank's attempts to control price increases.

A 46-year-old landlord named Mr Jones died at The Blossoms public house in Holyhead, and a 24-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder. The cause of death is yet to be released. Police are asking for people who were on board the number four Arriva Bus which left Bangor bus station at 14:00 GMT on Friday to come forward, as the bus may have relevant information regarding the incident.

The article invites readers to follow BBC News Entertainment on various social media platforms, including Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram, or send them story suggestions to entertainment.news@bbc.co.uk.

A red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van collided on the A713 near Carsphairn at approximately 10:40 on Friday, resulting in the deaths of both drivers, Antony Sztuka (50) and Scott Kennedy (46), both from Ayrshire. Police are seeking information from witnesses who may have seen a white flat-bed pickup truck in the area at the time of the crash. The road was re-opened around 18:45 hours.

Australian rower Sarah Tait, who won an Olympic silver medal in 2012, has been a source of inspiration for many in the sport due to her solid character and courage after being diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2013, as acknowledged by her coach and British rival Heather Stanning.

On the day of Afghan President Ashraf Ghani's inauguration and following the signing of a US-Afghan deal allowing US troops to stay in Afghanistan, the Taliban claimed responsibility for two suicide bombings, injuring military personnel and civilians in two separate locations in Kabul.

Daimler expects its full-year sales to exceed 100 billion euros, despite slower growth in Mercedes sales in China, as the company continues to see rising sales of Mercedes-Benz cars and Daimler trucks, with Mr. Zetsche forecasting continued growth in the major emerging markets and confidence in the company's overall performance and future potential.

The 10-year-old son of Denmark's Crown Prince Frederik was rescued from a rip current by lifeguard Nick Malcolm at Mermaid Beach, with the lifeguard receiving personal thanks from the Prince. According to fellow lifeguard Stuart Keay, the prince might not have survived without the timely rescue.

On Wednesday, a fire was reported on Elgin Road and Inchbroom Road, resulting in the unfortunate death of an elderly man. Police are conducting a joint investigation with firefighters, but initial findings suggest no suspicious circumstances were involved.

A specialized clinic at Surrey's Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC) has begun treating veterans with amputation-related medical complications, marking an expansion of services to offer them superior treatment, as they have made significant sacrifices for the nation's safety. The new program reflects a tertiary referral system within the NHS, allowing for the collaboration and knowledge sharing between the DMRC and existing NHS centers.

Enforcement cameras installed on a two-mile stretch of the M4 in Port Talbot have caught approximately 125 speeding drivers per day in less than a week, a decrease from the 700 daily violations during a pre-Christmas pilot period. The Welsh partnership aims to educate motorists about the dangers of excessive speed while emphasizing enforcement is a last resort after considering engineering solutions.

A Manchester-born man, living in Spain, is accused of secretly photographing his students, sending child pornography online, and possessing a large number of sexually explicit files involving minors. He was arrested as part of an Interpol investigation and is suspected of using a cloud storage service to share images. Authorities are currently trying to identify the victims in the images found on the suspect's electronic devices.

A seven-year-old sturgeon fish named Steve, which escaped from World of Water in Romsey, Hampshire during a flood, has been recovered after being found in a deep puddle near a car wash a mile away, manager Mark Bradbury stated that Steve was only slightly injured during his travels and was reunited with his tank mates.

Comedian and actor Chris Rock, known for his TV and film work such as Dr Dolittle and Madagascar, has filed for divorce from his wife, Malaak, after 19 years together, with a focus on privacy for their family, which includes two daughters.

A collision occurred on the motorway between Tamnamore, causing the closure in both directions, resulting in lengthy traffic delays. Police advise motorists to exit at either junction 12 or 15 depending on their destination, and urge anyone with information regarding the preceding events to contact them.

The French government has not yet received a response from the Vatican regarding the nomination of senior diplomat Laurent Stefanini as the new French ambassador to the Holy See, and the prolonged silence is being interpreted as a potential rejection due to his perceived liberal stance on homosexuality.

The Nasdaq experienced its largest one-day decline since April 2016, dropping 2.4%, as semiconductor, biotech, and other stocks decreased sharply; this occurred alongside a decline in U.S. durable goods orders, causing a drop in the Dow Jones (1.6%) and the S&P 500 (1.5%).

Vondrousova, the Czech 233rd-ranked player, advanced to the brink of the top 100 by defeating Kontaveit and Strycova in the Grand Prix Prague Open, while Coric, the 20-year-old Croatian 79th-ranked player, clinched his first ATP title by saving five match points to beat Kohlschreiber in the Grand Prix Hassan II in Marrakech.

Stoke City signs forward Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting, a 28-year-old with 200 Bundesliga appearances and international experience, as their fourth summer acquisition, having previously expressed interest in him four years ago.

A 56-year-old man with cerebral palsy, Seamus McCollum, who lived at a private nursing home in Randalstown, died last September, but his death was not initially treated as a murder case until an autopsy performed in April this year; a female individual is currently being questioned by the police in Antrim.

Heavy rains have deluged main streets in India's Tamil Nadu state, disrupting normal life, flooding 80,000 homes in neighboring Sri Lanka and prompting evacuations in Chennai, with the state government announcing a $75m relief fund and emergency response teams in action.

A McGill's 904 bus caught fire outside Largs on the A760 Kilbirnie Road with all passengers safely evacuated, including a partially-sighted woman and her daughter, who praised the driver's quick actions. Police Scotland closed the road and later re-opened it after removing the burnt-out bus.

Jake Ball, a 25-year-old cricket player, has started the 2016 County Championship season with six wickets in each of Notts' first two games, making him the leading wicket-taker. His performances have been so impressive that he has been named to lead Notts' bowling attack, alongside England's Stuart Broad, and has earned praise from both his coach and director of cricket. Despite his individual success, Notts suffered an eight-wicket defeat in their second match against Lancashire.

The article details the unveiling of a memorial stone, made from Jersey granite, in France, honoring 120 Jersey soldiers lost during the Battle of the Somme in World War I. A portion of the stone will be taken back to Jersey to be a part of a future memorial in Royal Square.

John Boyega, the former Theatre Peckham company member who portrayed Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens, is currently filming Star Wars Episode Eight, and he expressed his honor to give back to the theater where he started. The theatre's founder believes Boyega will be a tremendous inspiration for the young members given his success.

In the ongoing European Tour event, Thailand's Aphibarnrat and Fitzpatrick are tied at the top after impressive birdie performances, with several other players, including former world number ones Lee Westwood and Luke Donald,Hot on their heels. Notably, Bradley Dredge withdrew due to a viral infection, having been just two shots off the lead.

In the County Championship match, Middlesex has a strong position for their first win of the season, with Ashton Agar Voges scoring his first century of the season (128 not out) and Dawid Malan contributing 147 before getting out, despite the hosts losing early openers. Hampshire expects to salvage a draw with poor weather forecasted for the third day.

In an incident on Penilee Road on Friday, a 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy is in critical condition. A man police previously wanted to speak to in connection with the incident has been located in Dumfries and Galloway, and an area of Penilee Road is cordoned off with forensic investigations ongoing.

The three-bedroom red brick terrace house at 9 Newcastle Road, Wavertree, once home to a Beatle from birth to age five, was bought by an anonymous telephone bidder after a competitive bidding war, with a guide price of £150,000 to £250,000, and is located near Penny Lane, a famous Beatles landmark. The property received significant interest from both UK and international buyers.

A man, Aaron Joseph, has denied owning a dog that attacked and caused fatal injury to David Ellam while out of control in public, pleading guilty to possessing cannabis on the same date; trial set for 5 February, with Judge Peter Collier QC hoping for a sooner date.
A body thought to be that of 22-year-old Thomas Bebbington from Shrewsbury was discovered, approximately 10 miles away from where he was last seen entering a river near Dana Steps on 10th November.

Tiny five-week-old otters are being cared for with six daily feedings, with hopes they'll transition to a larger, outdoor enclosure during the summer and ultimately be capable of thriving on their own, including access to live food.

A 33-year-old mother-of-four, Joanne Thompson, was found dead in her Old Mill Court home in Newtownards, and police are seeking witnesses to a disturbance at a bonfire in Dakota Avenue on Monday, as well as anyone who saw unusual activity around her home the night before and early hours of Wednesday morning.

A record-breaking number of 2,270 black-tailed godwits (almost double the 2013 record) halted in a small field in Kilmoluaig, Hebrides, during their migration to Iceland this spring. Many were identified as having originated from France, Portugal, and Spain.

Former Rangers coach Jimmy Durrant will not be returning for pre-season training with the first team, as manager Mark Warburton plans to make changes to the coaching personnel, reflecting Durrant's repeated shifts between the first team and youth development squad throughout his tenure at Ibrox.
An albino deer, considered rare due to occurring once every 100,000 births, has recently been spotted, garnering much attention from visitors.

A 15-year-old student named Asad Khan from Bradford died three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heatson School and his family claim he was bullied. During the inquest, it was found that Asad had expressed feelings of "unsafe" in school and believed "life is hard" to a fellow student. The coroner is considering calling the student in for further evidence, with the inquest set to continue next month.

A 17th-century painting found at Rokeby Park, Barnard Castle, potentially originating from Durham, is of unique importance as it is the only representation of a coronation ceremony and has been in the park since at least 1880, but its artist, value, and origin remain unknown.

Macclesfield Town defeats Wrexham 3-0, with Danny Rowe, Mitch Hancox, and Danny Whittaker scoring for Macclesfield, while Wrexham's Jordan White misses a late penalty. The win moves Macclesfield up to seventh in the table, while Wrexham stay in 15th.

A new sponsorship deal has been struck between Total, a French oil and gas company, and the Confederation of African Football (Caf). The agreement will start from the 2017 Africa cup of Nations finals in Gabon. The actual value of the deal has not been disclosed, but Caf and Total see the partnership as a significant step towards advancing African football, aligning with Total's longstanding connection to the continent.

Spain coach Julen Lopetegui recalled Diego Costa and Juan Mata after Euro 2016 snub, opting to overlook Iker Casillas for World Cup qualifiers against Belgium and Liechtenstein, while also calling up 29-year-olds Cesc Fabregas, Pedro, and multiple Manchester United and Chelsea players.

A large, deliberate wildfire is currently spreading over a 5km area, across a border, causing concern and being treated as a threat to lives and properties, with at least 435 similar wildfires reported since May, according to Group Commander Brian Stanfield.

Irish cricketer Boyd Rankin, who briefly played for England between 2013 and 2014, is returning to Ireland's team, having agreed to a comeback after discussions with Cricket Ireland. He is eligible to play again due to ICC regulations and is available for upcoming matches, including the InterContinental Cup match with Papua New Guinea and the ICC World Twenty20 in India. Rankin is motivated by the possibility of Ireland achieving Test status and playing a part in this potential history.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, comprising of the Patient Client Council and created for sufferers and carers of rare diseases, seeks to enhance treatment and care through education, provision of specialized services, and advocacy, offering a platform for those impacted by rare diseases with no other means of representation.

Gloucester Cathedral plans to establish a girl chorister program, aiming to discover talented young singers from diverse backgrounds, with open auditions scheduled for April and a start in September, opening a new chapter in the cathedral's choral history.

Chelsea winger Pedro was taken to the hospital after suffering an injury during a game in Beijing, stayed overnight, and is expected to wear a protective mask when he returns to training, with the rest of the team now in Singapore for two upcoming matches.

Veteran cricketer James Taylor, who retired due to a heart condition in 2016, has returned to cricket coaching, working with Nottinghamshire and Yorkshire's academies. Meanwhile, former Northants captain David Sales is also joining the coaching staff, focusing on the technical aspects of the county's batters' game.

A man is facing multiple charges, including assault on police, for an incident on Whiterock Road observed by prescription pick-up waiters, including children, and he is scheduled to appear in Belfast Magistrates Court on December 5.

A yacht's engine failed a mile north-east of Muck Island on Thursday evening, prompting a volunteer crew from the Larne RNLI to launch two lifeboats and tow the yacht to Carrick Marina, with both inshore and all-weather lifeboats working together to assist the vessel's four occupants.

Ipswich clinched a thrilling victory over MK Dons in a match marked by multiple goals from David McGoldrick, Revell, Brett Pitman, and Kieran Agard (Varney), with the former three players scoring for Ipswich and the latter for MK Dons. Ipswich manager Mick McCarthy found the match exhilarating yet frustrating, while MK Dons manager Karl Robinson saw it as a microcosm of their season, acknowledging the need for improvement among some players.

A bridge collapsed on a London-bound motorway on August 27, causing serious injury to a motorcyclist and leading to a man from Darlington being charged with dangerous driving, causing serious injury, and criminal damage; the main route to the Channel Tunnel and Port of Dover was closed for two days while debris was cleared and the partially collapsed bridge was removed.

In the Spanish town of Platja d'Aro, a prank involving a fake celebrity chase turned into panic, as onlookers mistook selfie sticks for weapons, leading to a stampede, and resulting in eleven injuries, three hospitalizations, and the detainment of several German women for public order offences, with local authorities and the president of Catalonia expressing disapproval of the incident.

Two individuals, Sindyann Regis and Chevaze Mcgregor, are charged with the murder of a two-and-a-half-year-old boy named Jeremiah Regis, who was found with over 100 injuries, including a chest bite, at an address in Wolverhampton. The alleged crime took place on November 20, with the post-mortem examination revealing Jeremiah died of abdominal peritonitis caused by blunt force trauma. The case was adjourned until December with a provisional trial date set for 25 April. The family of the deceased boy released a tribute expressing their sadness, noting Jeremiah as a "lovely, quiet, innocent little boy" who will be missed.

A large gorse fire on Woodbury Common, Devon, has caused multiple injuries due to smoke inhalation, burns, and has fanned by high winds. The fire has been termed as a "very difficult incident" by the Chief Fire Officer, and firefighters are expected to remain at the scene overnight and into early Monday morning. Local evacuations and public warnings to avoid the area have been issued.

The British Speedway Promoters' Association, led by chairman Keith Chapman, has reached an agreement to secure the club's future, and a 15-year lease has been signed for the team's Beaumont Park venue. Upcoming meetings are planned to finalize the management structure, race night for the 2017 season, and other arrangements.

Elizabeth Bowe, aged 50, died three days after being severely injured in St Andrews, and her brother Charles Gordon, 51, appeared in court charged with her murder, with the Police Investigations and Review Commissioner (PIRC) launching an investigation focusing on the initial police response leading up to the incident.

A former Celtic and Motherwell midfielder, Jim O'Brien, has returned to Ross County on a two-year deal after a temporary stint last season, with the aim of helping develop the team's younger players. However, his availability for the upcoming Scottish League Cup encounter remains uncertain due to the necessity of international clearance.

In Division Two, Northants take early control of the game against struggling Durham, reducing them to 107 all out with regular wickets and dismissing key batsmen Keaton Jennings, Cameron Steel, Graham Clark, Paul Collingwood, and Michael Richardson. Northants themselves only managed 59-3 at the end of day one, with Rob Newton, Alex Wakeley, and Rob Keogh dismissed cheaply, but Max Holden and Chesney Hughes prevented further damage before an early close.

A 19-year-old New Zealander trails joint leaders Brooke Henderson and Lee Mi-rim by one stroke after two rounds, with multiple other players, including Catriona Matthew and Americans Gerina Piller and Brittany Lincicome, within reach at the halfway stage of the second women's major of the year, in a challenging conditions at the Sahalee Country Club.

Scotland manager Gordon Strachan has appointed former footballer Tommy Wright as an assistant, who will collaborate with Mark McGhee in the upcoming World Cup qualifiers. The move marks a second stint in the Scotland coaching set-up for Watson, who previously worked alongside Alex McLeish in the Euro 2008 qualifying campaign and played with both Strachan and McGhee at Aberdeen. He expressed excitement about the opportunity and confidence in the team's potential for progress.

Giants took an early lead against Belfast in a hockey game through Colin Shields, but goals from Ryan Martinelli, Mark Garside, and Alex Foster, coupled with efforts from Steve Saviano at the end of the first and second periods, left Belfast with a 5-1 deficit. Belfast have a game in hand on Coventry Devils, with both teams busy in the upcoming festive period.

In the 2016 Masters, Jordan Spieth suffered an unexpected quadruple-bogey seven on the par-three 12th hole, allowing fellow golfer Danny Willett to win his first major title, and emulating the 1996 Masters finale when Greg Norman surrendered a six-shot lead in a sudden collapse.

The article encourages readers to submit pictures to England's Big Picture initiative by emailing, sharing on social media (Facebook, Twitter, Instagram), providing recent images, complying with BBC's Terms and Conditions, and retaining copyright ownership while granting the BBC a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to publish and use the material, with the possibility of crediting the creator's name. Safety and legal considerations are emphasized in collecting media.

An eye specialist, Honey Rose, is on trial for gross negligence manslaughter in Ipswich Crown Court for the alleged failure to detect swollen optic discs during a routine eye test in 2012, which, according to the prosecution, led to the preventable death of Vinnie Barker.

Inflation in food prices increased by 4.9% in June, partially due to rising pork prices, while the overall inflation rate remains below the government's target. This development, along with concerns about a property bubble and global economic uncertainty, has led analysts and economists to predict that China will maintain its monetary policy in a neutral position, avoiding both interest rate cuts and tightening. Despite this, China still hopes to achieve an economic growth rate of 7.5% this year, which would mark the slowest growth in 23 years.

Former Newcastle United and Ivory Coast international Cheick Tiote, aged 30, passed away following a training collapse with his Chinese club Beijing Enterprises on June 5th. At his memorial, team-mates, family, and friends remembered Tiote, with Senegalese striker Cisse stating he had many life-sharing moments with the midfielder, who regarded his family as Cisse's own. Tiote played for Newcastle United for seven years, making over 150 appearances and three last season, before joining Beijing Enterprises in February.

In the fifth stage of the race, Slovak cyclist Peter Sagan won an uphill sprint, propelling him to his second victory, with Thibaut Pinot moving into second overall. Yates dropped out midway, while Geraint Thomas climbed to sixth overall for Team Sky, with two stages remaining, with overall leader remaining Nairo Quintana at the top.

Cuadrilla's fracking plans at Preston New Road, worth around £50 million, have been approved, despite a pending legal challenge by opponents. The firm plans to prioritize Lancashire for jobs, investment, and community initiatives, with approximately half of the funds expected to be spent locally. The site's building contract has been awarded to Bolton-based AE Yates Ltd and work is expected to start early next year, with an "independently audited tracker" monitoring Cuadrilla's pledges.

Three teenage boys from north-west London, missing in March amid concerns about plans to travel to Syria, were arrested after being stopped in Turkey, then released without charge. Their arrests followed a similar incident involving three east London schoolgirls who traveled to Istanbul and are believed to have joined Islamic State militants in Syria.

Hospital respiratory consultant Dr Christopher Davies criticized the purchase and fitting of a £22.95 blackout blind at the Royal Berkshire Hospital, which he considered overpriced, while the hospital's management team had reviewed and rejected the earlier quote for the item. NHS England is investigating the situation.

Swansea City's development squad, led by Adam King, secured the league title with a draw against Wolverhampton Wanderers in March, and won the cup final to amass 31 wins across all competitions in the 2016-17 season, while Swansea's senior team remained in the Premier League after Crystal Palace beat Hull 4-0.

Following severe winter storms in December 2013 that caused damage to a dune system at Barkby Beach in Prestatyn, a report suggests the dunes are re-establishing themselves naturally, but there's a concern about their narrowness. To strengthen the defenses, Denbighshire Council is considering creating a secondary dune system, as discussions have taken place with Natural Resources Wales regarding potential solutions to prevent a breach at this location. The flooding in December 2013 had forced about 400 people from their homes, particularly in Rhyl, one of the worst-hit areas.

The article announces that the FA Cup match between South Shields (Northern League Division One) and Bridlington Town (Northern Counties East League), taking place on 19 August at 12:30 BST, will be live-streamed across BBC Sport's digital platforms, including PC, mobile, and connected TV. Viewers can also watch the game live on BBC iPlayer, interact with the commentary team using #bbcfacup, and expect responses to messages during the game. South Shields, captained by Argentine former Sunderland and Middlesbrough full-back Julio Arca, made a successful Wembley appearance last season, winning the FA Vase final.

In Edinburgh, a 38-year-old man suffered serious but non-life threatening facial injuries in a targeted attack on Craigmillar Castle Road on Friday night, while a 49-year-old victim did not require medical attention. Police are encouraging residents to report any suspicious behavior or vehicles seen in the area at the time to help establish the full circumstances of the incident.

A 51-year-old woman, Pamela McLaggan, pleaded guilty to manslaughter for the death of Jonathan Baines, also known as "Willy", following an event at Market Rasen races in Gainsborough, and was remanded in custody before being sentenced on 21 December.

A 15-year-old boy was attacked and sustaining facial injuries, including an eye injury, by a man and woman in their 40s at Patterton station. The incident occurred at around 23:30 on Saturday 3 October, during the 23:05 service between Glasgow Central and Neilston. British Transport Police are urging anyone who witnessed the altercation or has information about the attack to contact them immediately.

A 17-year-old from Dewsbury was questioned by the North East Counter Terrorism Unit under the Terrorism Act in April, and two teenagers, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, are under investigation for suspected travel to Syria to join ISIS.

The Giants' forwards Boxill, Peacock, and Shields, along with netminder Stephen Murphy, are part of the 22-man squad for GB, aiming to progress to the final qualifying stage for the 2018 Winter Games in PyeongChang by beating Italy, Netherlands, and Serbia. Seventeen players from the previous 2015 World Championship (Division 1B) silver medal-winning squad are included, and as a side note, Cortina, a Serie A side, will play against the Belfast Giants during the tournaments, the first meeting between the teams in the Olympic Series.

Matthew Perry is allegedly taping a contribution for a tribute to the show's creator James Burrows, not a full "Friends" reunion as expected, while his former co-stars are set to participate in the special airing on NBC on 21 February. Meanwhile, Perry is returning to the West End with his play The End of Longing, a dark comedy about four people approaching middle age, which runs from 2 February to 14 May.

Despite a storied career before joining Burnley in 2013 that included stints at Manchester United, Preston, Derby, Blackburn, Wolves, and Oldham, and key contributions in helping the Clarets win the Championship title last season with 41 appearances, the 31-year-old saw his team suffer a Premier League defeat in their match against Swansea.

A Melbourne-based criminal lawyer and former cafe owner, Joe Acquaro, was reportedly shot dead, with investigators suspecting he might have been targeted by underworld bosses due to his associations with criminal accused of various offenses; this incident occurred against the backdrop of enduring underworld tensions in Melbourne.

On July 15, 2017, Air France Flight 374 from Paris to Vancouver carrying 294 passengers, was diverted to Prestwick, Scotland due to a slight smell of burning on board. A second aircraft was sent to return passengers to Charles de Gaulle Airport.

A severe weather warning has been issued for coastal areas and north-western parts of Wales, as Hurricane Gonzalo is set to bring strong winds and heavy rain to the UK starting on Monday night, with potentially destructive gusts exceeding 55mph inland and up to 70mph in exposed coastal areas, and Irish Ferries has cancelled some crossings due to the adverse weather conditions.

The article discusses concerns about hospital overcrowding and long wait times, particularly affecting children, as exemplified by the experiences of Lilly and Jake in a children's hospital in Sheffield.

A 34-year-old man from Poole was charged with causing grievous bodily harm, a 57-year-old woman from the same area was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm with intent and perverting the course of justice, and both are suspected in the death of 64-year-old Kenneth David Dickie who was found with a serious head injury at the Rockley Park site in Poole. The events transpired on May 8 and 10, and the woman was later bailed until July.

Former Manchester United forward Macheda will remain at Nottingham Forest for the rest of the season after failing to secure a transfer for Andre Moritz, as complications arose in releasing him from his Thai contract. Meanwhile, Forest midfielder David Vaughan has signed a new one-year deal.

The article reports that the body of missing worker Christopher Huxtable, who was one of four workers missing following a building collapse in February, was found on Wednesday, and his fellow workers formed a guard of honor as his body was driven off the site. Despite the discovery, two other workers, Ken Cresswell and John Shaw, are still missing. Swansea East MP Carolyn Harris expressed her sadness for the family and emphasized the ongoing uncertainty for the families of the two missing workers.

Bosnia-Herzegovina international is progressing from a hernia injury towards full match fitness, while Jordan Cousins has a season-ending quadriceps injury and Kazenga LuaLua is recovering from an ankle issue but remains a doubt for QPR. Bristol City aims to gain a win against QPR to potentially close the gap with Forest, Burton, and QPR in the standings.

Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano, who was selected by ESA in 2009 and traveled to the International Space Station in 2013, fondly recalled his spacewalk experience as "absolutely fantastic" and immensely enjoyable, with him feeling "giddy with excitement." His mission involved two spacewalks, orbiting Earth over 2,656 times, and traveling more than 110 million km.

A 16-year-old rugby player, Joe Arundel, who made 44 first-team appearances for the England Knights and scored 16 tries, is eagerly joining Hull FC, expressing excitement and some nervousness about the challenge and the pressure of joining a big club known for building a competitive culture and mentality for the present and future.

Ulster Bank is working aggressively to resolve an issue affecting approximately 600,000 payments, assuring no customers will suffer financial loss, following a recent system issue reminiscent of a 2012 IT meltdown that affected over 6.5 million customers earlier and led to a substantial fine.

In the 2016 Women's Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers played on Tuesday, Tanzania took a 2-0 lead against Kenya, but Kenya only managed a response through Christine Nafula, with Tanzania holding on to their advantage; meanwhile, Ethiopia defeated Uganda 4-1 in the play-off for third place.

McDonald's Japan faces potato shortage due to industrial action in America, resulting in rationed French fry portions at their over 3,100 outlets, while supermarkets also struggle with butter shortages.

The article announces that the upcoming Classic Horse Race on June 3rd will feature notable participants, including Permian and Khalidi, increasing its total purse to £1.625m, with Cracksman being the favorite, having previously beaten Permian in the Derby Trial, while an owner-breeder, Richard Aylward, is set to run his 1,000-1 outsider filly, Diore Lia, to fundraise for Great Ormond Street Children's Hospital.

Athletico Madrid footballer Antoine Griezmann, their top La Liga scorer, has a haematoma on his left foot, resulting in a missed friendly against Ivory Coast for France, after an X-ray ruled out a bone injury, as his team prepares to compete against league leaders Real at home on March 7th, trailing them by six points after 11 games.

A veteran rugby league prop player, Willie Mason, who has played for several NRL clubs including Canterbury and has international experience, is excited to join Laurent Frayssinous' Super League team, the Dragons, to help address their early season losses. Mason has a physical and aggressive style of play and brings a wealth of experience, including playing seven tests for the Kangaroos and 13 games for the Blues in State of Origin.

A new survey reveals an 11% increase of dog feces on UK beaches, with a sharp rise of 71% in Scotland, significantly affecting water quality and posing health risks for swimmers; the Marine Conservation Society notes the effort of pet owners cleaning up mess with bags but encourages proper disposal in designated bins.

The Supreme Court ruled that the 2013 government-introduced fees for employment tribunal claims were unlawful and indirectly discriminatory, and ultimately prevented workers from accessing justice, particularly women, as they ranged from £390 to £1,200 for a hearing and more for discrimination cases. This was deemed one of the biggest victories in employment rights in the country by Unison general secretary Dave Prentis.

In a football match, Wycombe Wanderers beat Dagenham & Redbridge with three goals, one after a sending off for each team. Despite playing with ten men for a part of the game, Dagenham showed good quality and resilience, with their manager expressing optimism about their potential to win multiple games and improve their position in the league.

Bee-eaters, native to southern Europe, have successfully nested for a second consecutive summer in the Low Gelt Quarry, drawing over 1,000 visitors to the RSPB viewpoint, with the chicks expected to fledge in the next few weeks.

A man's kayak capsized on the fast-flowing River Wey in Guildford at around 13:10 BST on Monday, prompting a search operation involving police, divers, firefighters, and ambulance crews. The public is urged not to enter the water themselves but to call 999, as a flood warning is in place and the river is a popular kayaking spot. The Wey Valley Kayak Club had previously warned of unsafe conditions on the river.

A young girl died at Rabat Zoo in Morocco after an elephant managed to throw a stone over a fence and injure her, an incident that is considered rare and unpredictable in captivity, according to the zoo and experts. The zoo stated the enclosure met international standards and that similar incidents have occurred in the U.S., while a video taken by a bystander shows the elephant waving its trunk and exhibiting the stone.

MP for North West Durham, Ms Glass, has been appointed to the shadow cabinet amidst a wave of Labour MP resignations calling for a leadership change, with her predecessor, Ms Powell, stating that the current leader's position has become "untenable." Ms Powell highlighted Mr Corbyn's decent, principled, and kind nature but concluded that his leadership was no longer effective, leading to calls for a new leader.

Chelsea leads the English Premier League with 59 points, 5 points separating them from second-placed Tottenham to sixth-placed Manchester United. 6 teams, including Manchester United, are considered strong title contenders, with Chelsea, Manchester City, Arsenal, and Liverpool making up the top six. Chelsea manager Conte warns against mistakes in the race and expresses concerns about teams at the bottom capable of winning and affecting the title race. Chelsea faces a challenging game against Burnley, who have won their last 7 home games.

Police and community support officers have implemented a dispersal order in Llangefni, allowing them to force troublemakers to leave, protect residents from anti-social behavior, and ensure the safety of young people from harm caused by alcohol misuse.

The Netherlands international, Marten de Roon, participated in 33 Premier League games for Middlesbrough in the 2016-2017 season, scoring five goals, and the club is reportedly interested in signing Chelsea midfielder Lewis Baker, as stated by manager Garry Monk.

The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, an award for humorous children's books established by Michael Rosen in 2008, will be relaunched in 2016 to mark the author's centenary celebrations, with a goal to make it more impactful in the future.

Frazier Glenn Miller Jr, a 74-year-old white supremacist, was sentenced to death for a 2014 shooting in Kansas that resulted in four deaths, including a grandson and his grandfather, the judge stating that his attempt to breed hate and terror had failed, with Miller responding by shouting "heil Hitler" in court.

The city council plans to introduce a larger scale self-service bike scheme of 500 bikes across the city starting from April 2017, with locations including district centers, universities, and strategic areas close to public transport, generating income through sponsorship and with no cost to the taxpayer, modeled after the "Boris bikes" scheme launched in London in 2010.

Despite missing the entire season so far and undergoing back surgery, Senegal international Sakho is now undergoing personal rehabilitation training and requires several weeks to get back to sufficient fitness levels before he can be considered available for selection in the Premier League.

The NI Residential Property Price Index shows a marginal 0.8% rise in average property prices in Q3 2020 compared to Q2, with a more substantial 7.3% increase in Antrim and Newtownabbey, and a smaller 2.1% increase in Ards and North Down. Terraced properties reported the highest annual rise at 7.1%, while apartments experienced a 4% increase. Around 5,200 property deals were completed in Q3.

The article discusses how the delivery of large wind turbine parts on rural roads in Dumfries and Galloway presents significant challenges, as demonstrated by two recent incidents – one successful and one resulting in a lorry and its cargo ending up in a ditch.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board suggested downgrading services, including maternity care, at one of its district hospitals due to staffing shortages; however, a legal challenge halted this plan for Glan Clwyd Hospital, leading to public consultations, mixed responses, temporary service changes proposed to ensure safety, and public meetings scheduled in September.

Du Preez scored a century (116 off 99 balls) and led South Africa to 272-6, while seamer Klaas dismissed Ireland's openers cheaply, resulting in Ireland being all out for 204 in an ODI match, with South Africa taking a commanding lead in the series.

Athlete Bethan Davey Peake, a silver medalist at the 2014 Commonwealth Games, is striving to surpass her own Welsh record of 4.40m and secure a Team GB spot in Rio, with the essential mark for Rio set by British Athletics at 4.50m.
A fire, believed to be deliberate, broke out at a building site involving scrapped railway sleepers in Llanwern, and lasted over 10 hours, with authorities launching an investigation.

A charitable event featuring a "Singing Bowl Concert" outside City Chambers on the Royal Mile, organized by Mercy Corps, Nepal Scotland Association, and the city council, collected funds for the relief efforts following the devastating earthquake in Nepal, where many members of the Nepal Scotland Association lost friends and loved ones.

Neil Lennon, Hibernian's coach, received a suspension from the touchline after remonstrating with referees during a Europa League game, which led to Hibs losing on penalties; the team is appealing the suspension imposed by UEFA.

A fire occurred 1,100m beneath the sea bed at the ICL UK Boulby mine, leading to some workers being hospitalized for smoke inhalation, with several unaccounted for. The Health and Safety Executive (HSE) has served an improvement notice upon the company, giving them until June 27 to comply, while the investigation continues. The mine is one of Europe's deepest, employing around 1,100 people.

A 23-year-old British man and a French tourist were caught naked and removed from the Unesco World Heritage site, Machu Picchu, for a minor morality offense; the Foreign Office is in contact with Peruvian authorities regarding the incident.

Ivan Rakitic, the 28-year-old Croatian international footballer currently playing for Barcelona, is set to sign a new contract on Friday, featuring a £109m buyout clause, extending his tenure with the club beyond his current 2019 contract end date.

A couple in Halstead suffered severe injuries after a two-hour ordeal of torture at their house on 26 April. The incident involved a break-in around 21:00 BST by three men, one black, of medium height and possibly in his 20s, and two whites. The police have a detailed description of the black suspect and are continuing to investigate the case. The woman remains critical, while the man is still receiving treatment. The crime was perpetrated with the threat of harm against family members.

The Wickerman Festival, taking place on 25 and 26 July at East Kirkcarswell Farm near Dundrennan, has announced Dizzee Rascal as their headliner for the opening night, with a diverse lineup that includes Martha Reeves and The Vandellas, The Zombies, Big Country, and The Feeling, with further headliner announcements to come for the Saturday night.

In the Aviva Premiership, Foden scored his third try in two matches as Saints beat Quins 24-3, with both players aiming to impress England coach Stuart Lancaster ahead of the Six Nations squad announcement, and Foden hoping for continued Saints representation in the national squad.

A fatal motorcycle collision occurred between a KTM motorcycle and a Vauxhall Zafira car in Dagenham, resulting in the 22-year-old motorcyclist's death, a 10-year-old passenger in the car sustaining serious injuries, and a 7-year-old passenger incurring minor injuries. The 38-year-old driver of the car was unaffected, and police are currently investigating and appealing for witnesses.

Pfizer, following the cancellation of its proposed $160bn merger with Allergan, has announced a deal to acquire California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals, whose flagship product, crisaborole, is a potential eczema treatment worth up to $2bn if approved by the US FDA, as it addresses a significant unmet medical need for a large patient population in the US (18-25 million) suffering from the condition. Anacor's stock price surged 57% following the news.

On Saturday at 23:00 BST, police responded to a street fight on Oxlow Lane, Dagenham, where they subsequently confiscated multiple weapons and cannabis and arrested two minors for possession of an offensive weapon and assaulting police, while no one was reported injured.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault after an attack on a 19-year-old woman at Gorsedd Gardens near Cardiff Civic Centre.

The Conservative MSP John Lamont resigned from the Ettrick, Roxburgh and Berwickshire constituency to challenge the SNP's Calum Kerr in a Westminster by-election, coinciding with concurrent local council and Holyrood elections in the area.

The EU Commission has approved the sale of beef from the UK, Ireland, France, and Germany to Canada, marking a significant shift following a ban due to the BSE crisis and set against a backdrop of industry hardship, decreased demand from China, and a €500m aid package for farmers. The move is part of a growing recognition of the EU's successful measures to eradicate BSE, with the US and Canada resuming imports under strict monitoring.

The European Commission plans to establish a common list of uncooperative tax havens and impose sanctions, following the Panama Papers revelations, but the process is expected to be complex due to conflicting national interests. Additionally, ministers have agreed to exchange company ownership information and crack down on banks and tax advisers aiding offshore tax evasion.

Archaeologists discovered Bronze Age burnt mounds, pottery fragments, and remains of kilns used for drying grain, including some belonging to the heating up of stones used for heating water, at Torvean, while constructing a new road for Highland Council to ease traffic flow through Inverness.
In the League One match, Oldham secured a victory through Main's goal after the hour mark, while Southend remained in 13th place.

Irish actor Lally, best known for roles in Glenroe, Ballykissangel, and various Irish language films, passed away peacefully after a brief illness, leaving behind his wife Peggy and their children Saileog, Darach, and Maghnus.

The Derby City Council, needing to save £79m over three years, initially planned to close Moorways Pool to save £350,000 annually, but after finding savings in "back-office areas" and management restructuring, they committed to keeping it open for a year, with the possibility of closure still pending if future government funding is not "fair".

Children previously held by Boko Haram are being detained, without proper legal process, in a military barracks in Maiduguri and there are concerns about entrapped minors, despite the recent release of some Chibok schoolgirls.

In the last week, Hearts footballer Alexander suffered a broken cheekbone, while teammate Gallacher twisted his ankle in training, potentially sidelining him for the upcoming Edinburgh derby. Coach Robbie Neilson is considering signing experienced goalkeeper Lee Hollis, formerly of Motherwell, to replace injured Neil.

A professional basketball player, Chelsey Lee, 26, is under investigation for allegedly fraudulently claiming Korean nationality by manipulating her and her father's birth certificates, after winning the WKBL's rookie of the year award in 2015-16. The league plans to nullify Lee's records, terminate the extra quota for international players with a Korean lineage, and implement stricter eligibility rules, following thecase and her team's actions.

The article outlines the release of an app that assesses Wi-Fi performance, suggesting many homes and offices could be running slower Wi-Fi than potential, with potential sources of interference listed. The article notes that there has been progress in the availability of super-fast broadband in the UK, with a significant portion of households using it for catch-up TV, online film rental, and video calls, but almost 8% of UK homes still cannot access speeds of 10Mbps or above, particularly in rural areas and small businesses.

Paul Pogba's emoji was displayed on boards at Old Trafford following his mixed performance against Liverpool, and he later acknowledged fans' support on social media. Zlatan Ibrahimovic, who scored the equalizer, praised Pogba for handling pressure and stated that he wants his team, Manchester United, to be top of the Premier League rather than accumulating personal accolades.

A man discovered a large floating metal object in a remote river in Salinopolis, Brazil, which was identified as debris from Europe's largest telecommunications satellite, Alphasat, launched from the Kourou base in French Guiana last July. The UK Space Agency confirmed that the object was a payload shroud from the Alphasat launch, and local authorities have agreed to retrieve it. The object, said to be the size of a car, initially caused some confusion and disbelief among locals.

The article discusses concerns raised by James Purnell that the decriminalization of non-payment of the BBC TV license could cost £200m, equivalent to the funding of BBC Four, CBBC, and CBeebies, and potentially lead to an increase in the license fee. The decision on decriminalization will not be discussed before charter renewal, but Labour MP John McDonnell has tabled a motion to reverse the decision to close BBC Three as a television channel.

In their first Premier Division game since 2008, Finhar Harps earned a decisive 2-1 win against Derry, with Ryan Curran and David Scully scoring for Harps, while Rory Patterson scored for Derry in the injury-time. Jordan Allan and Gareth McGlynn had early chances for Derry, but Harps midfielders Tony McNamee and Barry Molloy impressed in the contest.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has announced that issuers of securities using distributed ledger or blockchain technology, such as Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs), must register their offers and sales, as these transactions fall under existing regulations designed to protect investors and maintain market integrity. This decision comes following worries about the creation of an investment bubble in the ICO market and questions about how investors would be protected in the event of a venture failure. The action is in response to past concerns such as the hacking of the DAO, which resulted in the theft of $60m worth of digital coins.

Operation Anagram, formed by Strathclyde Police in 2006 after Peter Tobin's murder and rape of Angelika Kluk in Glasgow, also led to his convictions for the murders of Dinah McNicol and Vicky Hamilton. Despite being scaled back, it will remain active and anyone with information can still contact the team via email. The operation has provided some solace to the families of the victims, and Det Sup David Swindle is proud of its role in bringing closure to some bereaved families. Tobin is currently serving three life sentences for these murders.

In the Australian Grand Prix, Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel emerged victorious over Lewis Hamilton, with Hamilton expecting a potential turnaround at the Chinese Grand Prix on Sunday. He admitted Ferrari outperformed Mercedes in Melbourne, but acknowledges it will be a closely contested season with implications switching back and forth between the teams. Both drivers acknowledge that Ferrari has its strengths, but Mercedes remains the team to beat.

Southwark Crown Court heard that Mr Clifford, a former celebrity manager, is on trial for allegedly exposing himself and forcing a woman to perform a sex act, which he denies; his interview with police includes multiple "no comment" responses, and his trial has been adjourned until Monday, when he is due to give evidence.

Ospreys coach Steve Tandy anticipates a physically intense match following an entertaining loss in Bordeaux, aiming to reduce the points gap between them and the Scarlets in the Pro14, with New Zealand scrum-half Brendon Leonard remaining questionable due to a shoulder injury.

The annual Diwali celebration on Leicester's Golden Mile, known for its large firework display, attracted a significant number of people from various backgrounds, with the event being considered one of the largest Diwali parties outside India. The celebration, which includes Rangoli street art, stage entertainment, and other citywide events, promotes unity and sharing of joy beyond the Hindu faith.

Rosie's Helping Hands, a charity founded by Karen and Mr. Ross in memory of their daughter Rosie Ross, who was tragically killed in 2001, aims to raise £15,000 during its final annual Rosie's Walk, with plans to wind down the charity by summer 2017. The funds raised have already contributed to improving a children's ward at Walsall Manor Hospital through the installation of a pirate-themed play area, providing a positive outlet for children dealing with hospitalization.

Macmillan Cancer Support and Cwm Taf Health Board are planning to build a new specialist palliative care unit at the Llantrisant site, providing high-quality care for incurable cancer patients, at a cost of £5 million, with the potential to ease transfer difficulties and distress experienced by patients traveling between hospitals. If approved, construction could start later this year, with an opening date anticipated for late 2018 or early 2019.

The Top 10 destinations for 2018 as chosen by travelers include Peru's Choquequirao, Snowdonia in Wales, North Island of New Zealand, the Azores in Portugal, North Wales, Northern Australia, Aysén in Chile, the Tuamotus in French Polynesia, the Georgian Coast, Perak in Malaysia, and Skellig Ring in Ireland. Lonely Planet Director Tom Hall describes North Wales as a "destination that can be difficult to find on the world stage." He also notes that North Wales offers a wide range of activities suitable for travelers. The Welsh Economy Minister, Ken Skates, stated that the North Wales area has witnessed a boost in the first-time visitors coming to Wales, demonstrating a warm welcome, culture, and history of the region.

The Church of England and the Church of Scotland have committed to growing together in communion and strengthening their partnership in mission, as outlined in the Columba Declaration found within the Growth in Communion, Partnership in Mission report. The declaration allows for clergy and laypeople to be welcomed into each other's churches when moving across the border, recognising their separate constitutional responsibilities in the UK.

A severely injured Afghan bombing victim and decorated soldier, L/Bdr Parkinson, who carries the Olympic torch in 2012 despite his injuries, experiences an overwhelming response on Facebook with thousands of friend requests, but his personal page limit won't allow him to accept all of them. His story of determination, humor, and charitable work has led to an influx of support, including increased mail and e-mail traffic, and requests for him to visit various locations with the torch. Facebook suggests he consider changing to a public figure page or using the subscribe option to manage his constantly expanding online community.

A significant drug smuggling operation involving five individuals, allegedly including a prince, was intercepted at Beirut airport, with two tonnes of Captagon pills discovered, marking the largest seizure of its kind at the airport. The captagon pills, which are commonly consumed in the Middle East, are said to have fueled conflicts, particularly in Syria, and have been linked to substantial revenue generation for producers.

The Sexual Offences, Exploitation and Child Abuse Command is conducting an investigation and Kids Company, a charity run by Camila Batmanghelidjh, is cooperating, prioritizing the safety of its clients while operating with robust internal policies to protect them. The police and NSPCC are asking for any relevant information from the public.

The Queen, who turns 90 this week, is described by her cousin Margaret Rhodes as being full of laughter, having a sense of humor, and able to imitate both the Norfolk and Scottish accents. On her birthday, she will spend time at Windsor Castle, where gun salutes will be held across the UK, and she will unveil a plaque on the Queen's Walkway.

The United Nations Agency for Human Settlements' report indicates that Latin America, the world's most urbanized region, experiences extremely high income inequality, with the richest 20% earning 20 times more than the poorest 20%. The region, which is at the end of an era of urban expansion, has shown reductions in poverty, indigence, and unemployment, and is positioned to transition towards a focus on quality of life, equity, and sustainability, particularly addressing the cited challenges of job deficits and labor informality.

A Carmarthenshire Labour councillor, Tegwen Devichand, is under investigation for sharing a Facebook post that was initially posted by the far-right group Britain First, advocating for the death penalty for sex predators. She denies sharing the post and opposes the death penalty. The post, about choose in education, has been controversial and sparked accusations of working with UKIP to undermine the council's decision. Devichand is also complaining about a "hate campaign" against her, while Plaid Cymru is calling for swift action to address the issue within the Labour party.

The Iraq War Families Campaign Group, led by relatives of British soldiers killed in the Iraq War, launched a crowdfunding campaign to seek legal action against individuals responsible for the conflict, following the publication of the Chilcot report. After quickly raising the initial £50,000 target, they are now fully funded to analyze the report and determine whether legal action against key figures involved in the invasion would be successful.

Syed's defense team is given the opportunity to reopen the case for the 1999 murder of Hae Min Lee, as a judge in Baltimore allows for the submission of new evidence, including questions about the accuracy of mobile phone records used in the original trial and the testimony of a potential alibi witness who claims to have seen Syed in a library at the time of the crime, a fact overlooked by his original legal team.

A 16-year-old boy who attended a party in Dundee last November, pulled a machete on a taxi driver upon their return to the party, prompting one of his friends to steal the driver's change. The attacker had previously served custodial sentences for assaults committed when he was 14 and 15. The boys will be sentenced next month after at least one of them, the perpetrator, pleaded guilty to assault, and one admitted theft.

John Clancy, a long-time Labour councillor, has been elected as the new leader of Birmingham City Council, beating out rival Penny Holbrook by a single vote, after five previous attempts. Clancy plans to focus on providing new homes and improving social housing, expanding regeneration outside the city centre, widening access to free school meals for primary school children, and making smarter financial decisions. The council has been under scrutiny from a government-appointed independent panel due to issues raised during an inquiry into the so-called Trojan Horse letter.

The interview for June's Empire magazine featuring actor Moore discussed his early meetings with Bond director Guy Hamilton, where they aimed to avoid deliberate comparisons to Sean Connery, while the new Bond film, Skyfall, starring Daniel Craig, is set for release in October, featuring Aston Martin DB5s in a car chase, and Connery's authentic portrayal of the character was considered revolutionary in the series by producer Barbara Broccoli.

Witches' marks, believed to offer protection during the era of widespread belief in witchcraft and the supernatural, are symbols found near entrances of medieval buildings. These marks, often taking the form of patterns like the Daisy Wheel or letters such as AM or M, were intended to confuse and trap evil spirits. Historic England encourages documentation of these marks, found in buildings, churches, and even caves across England, to learn about past beliefs and rituals.

During Prime Minister's Questions, Jeremy Corbyn compared Theresa May's stance on Brexit negotiations to Baldrick, the dim-witted servant from the comedy show Blackadder, saying her claim of having "no plan" reflects Baldrick's infamous catchphrase. This comparison sparked a response from Tony Robinson, who played Baldrick, causing him to tweet about the comparisons and be approached in his hairdresser's.

The Liverpool County Court ruling, in a case involving Jet2 and passenger Kim Allen, has rejected airlines' arguments to delay compensation payments for flight delays, stating "justice delayed is justice denied". This decision is significant for thousands of similar claims in the UK, and law firms are advocating for improved compliance with EU regulations mandating airlines to pay compensation for cancellations and delays.

Jamie Dimon, CEO of JP Morgan, has escalated his threat to move hundreds more jobs out of the UK to Dublin and Frankfurt, stating that the UK's control over additional job losses is no longer certain due to the EU's potential regulations post-Brexit, while French President Edouard Philippe has promised a pro-banker environment in France to attract financial institutions.

China disputes reports of deploying surface-to-air missiles on a claimed disputed island in the South China Sea, stating it has the right to self-defense under international law. The U.S. and other nations have expressed concern over China's militarization of the region, with satellite images appearing to confirm China has armed Woody Island. Conversations about the increasing tension in the South China Sea were held at a meeting of Southeast Asian regional leaders.

Spider jumping footage reveals they use silk draglines to stabilize and brake during jumps, enabling them to land poised for prey capture. This flexible, adjustable silk tension is seen as a potential inspiration for future robot designs.

The Supreme Court ruled that the UK government is not legally bound to consult with devolved legislatures, including Wales, when triggering Article 50 of the EU treaty, but there is a possibility that the Welsh Assembly may have a vote on the issue, influencing but not vetoing the process.

The Co-op Bank, under pressure to meet Bank of England regulations, is nearing a recapitalization agreement with existing investors, with discussions centering around separating its pension fund from the Co-operative Group's scheme due to its $8bn liabilities.

The article discusses a dispute between Tidal Lagoon Power (TLP) and Natural Resources Wales (NRW) over claims that the Swansea tidal lagoon project could cause significant fish deaths. TLP denies the NRW's estimated 21% of salmon and 25% of sea trout dying each year, stating their computer modelling shows only a worst-case scenario of 2% of fish species dying; NRW maintains that their figures are based on the best available evidence.

The article summarizes various memorable blunders in a British business-themed reality TV show, highlighting moments of sexism, poor decision-making, and comical mishaps, all of which audiences find entertaining because they can imagine doing better themselves.

The Home Affairs select committee found that the UK's immigration cap, limiting recruitment from outside the EU, has been "counter-productive" as it has stimulated recruitment from EU countries, and has not effectively reduced net migration. Additionally, the cap has reportedly caused a potential crisis in the NHS due to rejections of visa applications for nurses with job offers in the UK, and the government has had to implement emergency measures to allow for continued recruitment.

An off-duty British soldier named Matthew Boyd was fatally attacked outside a bar called The Cellar in Brecon, Wales, after which his attacker, Jake Vallely, was found guilty of manslaughter. However, Vallely's friend Aaeron Evans was cleared of any involvement. The trial heard that Vallely had been on a drinking binge and boasted about being the "hardest man in Brecon" prior to the attack. The family of the deceased, who served with the Royal Gibraltar Regiment, described Boyd as an "all-rounder" with a "promising career ahead of him." They also expressed their appreciation for the love and support received from the Brecon community, referring to them as the "strongest people in Brecon."

The BBC, in partnership with This Place, has developed a brainwave-reading headset that allows users to select and operate BBC's iPlayer on-demand platform by concentrating or relaxing their minds, with potential future applications for helping those with disabilities.

The Chief Inspector of schools in Wales, Meilyr Rowlands, stated that the focus on certain performance measures discourages schools from providing adequate support to more able students, potentially stifling their progress. The Welsh Government agrees and is implementing changes to address this issue and aims to raise academic standards for all young people.

The forthcoming album, Out Among the Stars, features previously unheard recordings by Johnny Cash, recorded in 1981 and 1984, and includes duets with June Carter and Waylon Jennings. These recordings were found in a vault in 2012, marking the fourth posthumous release since Cash's death in 2003. John Carter Cash, according to the BBC, believes these unreleased recordings are a work of art and are worth releasing as they would add to Cash's existing legacy of selling over 90 million records, with known hits like Ring of Fire and I Walk the Line.

The tribunal ruled that Maria McKeith was unfairly dismissed by the Ardoyne Association due to her role as a primary carer for her disabled daughter, a violation of the Disability Discrimination Act 1995. The Court of Appeal upheld the decision, awarding her compensation for injury to feelings, loss of earnings, and interest. Employers were reminded of their responsibilities under the law to protect against discrimination towards disabled individuals and their primary caregivers.

Scottish midfielder Kenny Dorrans, with a history at West Bromwich Albion and most recently Norwich City, has signed a three-year deal with Rangers, making him the ninth summer signing for Pedro Caixinha, following in the footsteps of Bruno Alves, Daniel Candeias, Carlos Pena, Eduardo Herrera, Dalcio, Ryan Jack, Alfredo Morelos, and Fabio Cardoso. Dorrans expressed his excitement about joining the iconic club.

Scottish teams Team Brewster and Team Muirhead, led by Glen Muirhead (brother of winning skip Eve), defeated David Murdoch's Olympic silver medallists and Hannah Fleming's team respectively, to secure the men's and women's berths for the European Championships in Scotland. Both teams are eager for the home event, with Glen Muirhead's girlfriend, Anna Sloan (playing third for Team Muirhead), making her return from injury this week.

A local councillor, Pierre Oxley, called for a scrutiny meeting next Tuesday regarding the Holland Haven-to-Clacton defences, accusing the council of not being clear on the beach's sand-to-shingle ratio, while the council's head, Peter Halliday, insists they have been transparent throughout the process.

John Nelms, co-owner of Dundee Football Club, announced a land use application will soon be submitted for land in Camperdown Park, aiming to enhance the club, as they are dealing with various issues in a "19th century building," and have incurred significant costs for maintenance.

Despite a close finish in the second stage of the Criterium du Dauphine, Team Sky's Chris Froome trails overall leader Alberto Contador by 13 seconds, with stage winner Jesus Herrada in between them. Froome will focus on the Tour de France ahead of the Olympic road race.

The article discusses the discovery of the bodies of ex-EastEnders star Sian Blake, 43, and her two sons, Zachary, 8, and Amon, 4, at their family home in London on Tuesday; the police's missing persons inquiry was launched following concerns about Blake's welfare and information from the NSPCC; the case is now being treated as a triple murder inquiry; police are seeking Arthur Simpson-Kent, the children's father and Blake's partner, as a suspect, as he is believed to have traveled to Ghana; the IPCC has promised to investigate the Met's handling of the case.

Due to delayed matches on multiple courts, Wimbledon organizers have decided to play on the middle Sunday for only the fourth time in history, in order to avoid sections of the draw becoming too far apart and to maintain a fair tournament schedule.

Dutch football manager Dick Advocaat has decided to leave English club Sunderland after guiding them to safety from relegation, despite initially agreeing to stay only until the end of last season. His departure follows a trend of managers arriving to save Sunderland, only to depart in the next season.

Russia's economy is projected to experience a 0.8% decline in GDP next year, following a 0.6% growth in 2014, due to the impact of reduced energy exports, oil price slump, and Western sanctions, which have resulted in a 6% drop of the rouble to 57 to the dollar on Monday, and a loss of half its value against the dollar this year. To counteract the economic downturn, President Putin has taken measures such as doubling the deposit guarantee for bank accounts and giving the central bank the power to recapitalize Sberbank, the country's largest retail bank.

Presidential candidate Raila Odinga has accused Kenya's electoral authorities of fraud and is taking the dispute to the Supreme Court, claiming to have evidence of massive irregularities, while international observers have described the election as free and fair, and the international community calls for calm amid fears of potential violence.

A 60-year-old scuba diver suffered a cardiac arrest while diving at Agincourt Reef in Far North Queensland, and despite CPR efforts, he could not be revived, making it the third tragedy in two days involving French tourists at local reefs.

The UK, Scottish governments, and Dundee City Council have agreed a 3.7 million pound public service obligation (PSO) contract to continue Loganair's operation of the air service between Dundee and London Stansted for another two years, with UK Aviation Minister and Scotland's Transport Minister expressing optimism about the role it will play in boosting trade, tourism, and at-risk connectivity between smaller regional airports and London.

The World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) begins offering its video streaming service in mainland China, targeting a potentially vast market, with the outlet provided by PPTV. The network incorporates major live events, original series, and classic matches, hoping to find success by discovering local stars and potentially capitalizing on their fame. Other sports have also attempted to make inroads in China, but industry experts caution that the process might not be as straightforward as it seems.

Three men, including a West Midlands police officer, are being questioned for conspiracy to pervert justice and related offenses, following a hoax tip-off suggesting an officer was to be kidnapped as part of a terrorist plot, which led to a heightened state of alert for the West Midlands police and subsequent unnecessary precautions.

Ireland secured a 4-1 victory over Poland in a must-win match of the World League 3 quarter-finals, with goals by McKee (twice), Magee, and O'Donoghue. The winners advanced to the semi-finals against Wales, with France facing Scotland. Ireland coach Craig Fulton praised the team's performance and noted they could have scored more goals.
