Philip Craig, a 38-year-old from Leeds, has been sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum of 25 years for stabbing and killing Christopher Laskaris, a 24-year-old man with Asperger's Syndrome and bi-polar disorder, in Leeds in November. Craig had pleaded guilty to burglary and was already serving a three-year sentence for the crime, which was to be served concurrently. Craig's victim's body was discovered on November 17, and Craig had returned to the flat to steal items, such as a TV, games console, and guitars. The court heard that Craig exploited and abused Mr. Laskaris, whose death had a devastating impact on his family. A second man, Dempsey Pattison, 22, was previously charged with the murder but had his case discharged in February.

The Metropolitan Police has closed a reinvestigation into the 2010 death of Kester David, a man believed to have been killed for working as a police informant, acknowledging previous failings in their initial investigation, including not checking CCTV or interviewing witnesses promptly. Despite numerous appeals, no arrests have been made in connection with his death.

In 2015, football had the highest total attendance with 43.4 million, followed by three horse racing events in the top 10. Rugby union improved with the Rugby World Cup, reaching 7.5 million. Notably, Wimbledon was the most attended individual event with just under half a million spectators. British Grand Prix in Formula 1 had the highest attendees-per-event-day. Two new events, MotoGP's British Grand Prix and Badminton Horse Trials, replaced the Ryder Cup and Aintree Grand National in the top 10. Overall attendances increased by 6% compared to the previous year, although the total was lower than the record set in 2012 due to the Olympic and Paralympic Games in London and the Rugby World Cup in 2015. Future major UK sports events include the UCI Track Cycling World Championships, the European Aquatics Championships, and the FIH Women's Champions Trophy in hockey.

Beyoncé had the highest-grossing year of her career in 2013-2014, earning an estimated $105 million, followed by Taylor Swift at $64 million, Pink at $52 million, Rihanna at $48 million, and Katy Perry at $40 million, according to Forbes, based on income from touring, record sales, publishing, merchandise sales, endorsements, and other ventures. Additional artists mentioned who missed out on a top 10 spot include Madonna, Nicki Minaj, and Alicia Keys.

The Scottish National Party claims it has more MP support than Labour Leader Jeremy Corbyn, but Speaker John Bercow maintains Labour is still recognized as the official opposition due to the rulebook and recent events.

The villagers of Crickhowell successfully launched a bid to buy The Corn Exchange and prevent its conversion into a supermarket, with plans to transform the building into independent shops with flats above, under the management of a new company called Corn Exchange Crickhowell Ltd.

RIT Capital will not make a formal bid for Alliance Trust, which is engaging in a strategic review that could potentially result in a sale or outsourcing, and the ongoing process at Alliance Trust is exempt from the stock market's takeover and merger procedures.

Alexis Scott, 39, a former Police Community Support Officer, was convicted for tricking long-haul airline passengers into thinking they had excess cash on them during flights in April 2013. She was sentenced to time in prison, which would separate her from her young daughter, due to the severity and nature of the crime, as well as the violation of public trust.

Educational platform TrueTube has received three award nominations for its drama and learning categories, notably for the films Refugee and Katie. Horrible Histories, meanwhile, earned three nominations for its special Shakespeare episode, with the Bafta Children's Awards recognizing various other programs and films in a range of categories such as comedy, animation, writing, and feature film. The awards ceremony will take place at the Roundhouse in London on 20 November.

Lady Mary Soames, the last surviving child of Sir Winston Churchill, bequeathed most of her collection of Churchill's artworks, including "Coast Scene near Cannes" and "View From a Bathing Hut at the Miami Surf Club," to the National Trust, Houses of Parliament, and Churchill War Rooms. These works were accepted in lieu of inheritance tax, and will be displayed in significant locations tied to Churchill's life, as per Culture Minister Ed Vaizey's statements. The works' display is timed to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Churchill's death.

An ex-investigator from the ombudsman's office was arrested for alleged theft of sensitive security documents containing information potentially endangering lives. This has raised concerns among the police federation, officials, and a local politician about the ombudsman's office's handling of sensitive material and the fairness of investigations. The police have initiated a criminal investigation and temporarily suspended the sharing of future sensitive material to the ombudsman's office for a review of security protocols.

Phyllis Schlafly, a conservative advocate and outspoken opponent of feminism and abortion, is remembered as an "iconic American leader" who played a significant role in blocking the Equal Rights Amendment and creating a political climate that helped Republicans win elections, particularly Ronald Reagan's presidency in the 1980s. Her death was announced by the conservative group Eagle Forum she had founded, and she was publicly endorsed by Donald Trump during his 2016 presidential campaign.

A 23-year-old rugby player, who has been named Championship player of the season, is leaving Bristol at the end of the season to move back to Wales, citing a desire to test himself and develop further in preparation for potential selection for the Welsh national team, with Newport Gwent Dragons and his former team, Ospreys, reportedly interested in his services.

The article details the trial of two people smugglers, Mufawaka Alabash and Asem Alfrhad, charged with the death of Syrian toddler Alan Kurdi, who became a symbol of the refugee crisis. Despite being found guilty of people smuggling, they were acquitted of causing death through deliberate negligence. Alan's family, including his brother Galib and mother Rihan, also lost their lives attempting the same crossing. The discussion revolves around the ongoing migration crisis, with Donald Tusk proposing the idea of sending migrants back to the Greek islands from which they entered Turkey.

Former Milan station chief Robert Lady, convicted in absentia for his involvement in the abduction and "extraordinary rendition" of Egyptian cleric Abu Omar, who was allegedly tortured, was released and boarded a US-bound flight according to American officials, after being arrested near Panama's border with Costa Rica. The Milan trial was the first involving the CIA's practice of transferring suspects to countries where torture is permitted, which has been condemned by human rights groups as a violation of international agreements.

The article reports that during January 2017, Edinburgh Airport experienced a significant 11.7% year-on-year increase in passenger traffic, most notably in international flights, due to the launching of 27 international services in 2016. Glasgow Airport reported an 8.4% rise, with strong demand for routes to Toronto, New York, and Dubai, and a 21.4% increase in EU-scheduled traffic. Aberdeen International Airport, despite a 1.7% drop in overall passengers, had its lowest decline in nearly two years, with increased domestic traffic (0.6%) and new flights to Faro, Riga, and the Faroe Islands planned for later in the year.

The most-watched video on YouTube, Gangnam Style by Psy, has surpassed the previous view limit of 2.147 billion views, prompting YouTube to update its counter system to a 64-bit integer with a new maximum view limit of 9.22 quintillion views.

England, despite a rocky start with losses to West Indies and a near-collapse against Afghanistan, are aiming to secure their spot in the World Twenty20 semi-finals by defeating Sri Lanka. The match, scheduled for Saturday, is crucial for England as they seek to combine strong performances in batting and bowling consistently. Alex Hales is improving but his availability for the match remains uncertain due to a back injury. Sri Lanka, currently in second place in the group but undefeated since their last match, have struggled with their middle order batting but remain a formidable opponent due to their quality spinners.

Inrix Roadway Analytics, in a survey of Britain's roads in September 2016, found that Edinburgh is second, Glasgow third, and London first in the list of the most congested cities, with Edinburgh's 455 traffic hotspots projected to cost drivers £2.8bn by 2025, while Glasgow's 357 hotspots could cost £2.3bn over the same period. Nationwide, the research predicts a loss of £61.8bn due to congestion by 2025, with London having the most traffic "pinch points" in Europe, followed by Rome and Paris. The report emphasizes the importance of identifying traffic hotspots and analyzing their causes to combat congestion.

In the 44th minute of a friendly, a deflected shot by Norway's Nordtveit off Sammy Clingan's heel beat keeper Lee Camp to give Norway a late first-half lead. Northern Ireland struggled to find a response despite a bright start, and goals from substitutes Elyounoussi, Ruud, and a fine effort from O'Neill's men extended Norway's lead, leaving Northern Ireland winless in 14 friendlies.

Brussels, Belgium remains on high alert due to potential Paris-style attacks, as a suspect in the Paris attacks is still at large, and authorities have issued an arrest warrant for Mohamed Abrini, who was allegedly seen with another suspect days before the Paris attacks. Hundreds of police and soldiers patrol the city, and transportation resumed with some lines closed. The suspected ringleader of the attacks, Abdelhamid Abaaoud, reportedly had connections to the Bataclan theatre and La Defense business district. France and the US reaffirm their commitment to eradicating IS.

There were multiple fatal explosions in Zaventem Airport and Maalbeek metro station in Brussels on March 22, causing numerous casualties, prompting national mourning and increased security measures across several countries. The Islamic State group has claimed responsibility for the attacks, which follow similar incidents in Paris in November 2015.

Sheffield City Council's Green Party councillor, Alison Teal, faces potential legal action for her involvement in protests against the city's tree felling program; the council asserts that the removal of street trees is lawful and necessary, having faced months of disruption by a handful of protesters, with works continuing to be disrupted despite previous warnings.

In New Zealand, about 300 whales have died at Farewell Spit, South Island, marking one of the largest mass beachings recorded. Rescue efforts involving locals and conservation department staff are underway to save the survivors. The cause of the stranding is unclear, but it's suspected that old age, illness, injury, and navigational errors may play a role. The incident has one of the highest rates of strandings in the country, with many occurring at Farewell Spit due to its shallow waters confusing and hindering whale navigation.

Experienced prop forward Brian Mujati, with a history of playing at high levels, has been signed by the Ospreys to provide injury cover for their current tight heads, Dmitri Arhip and Ma'afu Fia, due to their unavailability and Rhodri Jones' involvement in the Wales squad. Coach Steve Tandy expects Mujati to have a significant impact, as the injury situation warrants immediate reinforcements in this crucial position, with the team having numerous games remaining in the PRO12 and Challenge Cup.

The Gwynedd council has decided to proceed with establishing a new Church in Wales campus at Ysgol y Berwyn in Bala, despite opposition from community members, with the merging of Ysgol Bro Tegid and Ysgol Beuno Sant, while the Church in Wales maintains it remains committed to providing the best education for the area's children.

The article discusses a disagreement between Oxfordshire County Council and the county's five district councils over a proposal to consolidate all local services under one council. The county council advocates for this move to potentially save £100m over five years, while district councils prefer a three-council approach and advocate for an elected mayor at the county level. The dispute is seen as a "turf war," with each group claiming their plan would be more beneficial for securing funds from central government. The public is being asked for input before a final decision is made by the county council's cabinet on March 14th.

Edinburgh Rugby, led by Dickinson, aims to win the remaining five matches in a tough run-in to have a shot at playoffs or the top six, starting with a challenging away game against Newport Gwent Dragons and continue with Zebre, Leinster, Munster, and Cardiff Blues. Edward aims to eliminate errors and finish opportunities to improve their performances, following recent losses in five out of six games under their coach, Solomons.

The Northern Ireland Bat Group, led by Karen Healy, is caring for an unprecedented number of grounded, malnourished, and injured young bats. Volunteers are hand-raising and nursing these bats back to health before releasing them back into the wild. These bats are commonly found in uncommon places, with the group receiving countless calls daily. Bat conservation is essential due to their economic value as pest controllers and debunking common misconceptions about their nocturnal nature and feeding habits.

The Supreme Court is currently considering the federal law limiting gun ownership for individuals convicted of domestic violence, and during the second week of oral arguments since the death of Justice Antonin Scalia, Justice Clarence Thomas asked a lawyer if any law violation suspends a person's constitutional rights. This marks Thomas's return to questioning in court after a long silence.

British travel company Responsible Travel, after watching a BBC programme, decides to remove half a dozen trips involving zoos from their offerings of 3,500 tours. The firm's boss, Justin Francis, argues that keeping animals in zoos is inhumane and they are relics of the past, as most animals are not endangered and few endangered species have been successfully reintroduced into the wild after being kept or bred in captivity. The decision is welcomed by the wildlife charity Born Free Foundation.

A child of primary school age has been found deceased at a home in Faringdon, leading to a 40-year-old woman's arrest on suspicion of murder. The community is shaken, with local authorities increasing police presence to provide reassurance, while they urge any with information to contact them.

A British suspect, known as BM, is facing charges for allegedly breaching the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPim) for failing to contact a monitoring company and report to a police station twice in January, marking what appears to be the first alleged breach of this system since its implementation in 2012. The Home Office has chosen not to comment on the specific case. TPims replace control orders and include various measures, such as stay-at-home curfews, daily police station visits, travel restrictions, and contact bans. Despite criticism that TPims have weakened public protection against terrorism due to their two-year maximum term, no other such breach court cases have been reported. The defendant was granted unconditional bail; a hearing will be held on July 2 for a plea and case management but no trial date has been set.

Qualcomm, the world's largest supplier of smartphone chips, agreed to China's largest corporate fine, lowering its royalty rates on patents used in China's mobile phone market. This move is expected to benefit Chinese smartphone makers Xiaomi and Huawei. Qualcomm expressed satisfaction with the approved rectification plan, making royalties based on 65% of the phones' selling price in China. This resolution removes uncertainty for the company in China and will allow it to focus on growth opportunities in the expanding high-speed 4G market, contributing significantly to Qualcomm's global revenue.

Michelle Mellotte, 61, has been barred from practicing as a doctor in the UK, following a police investigation and medical tribunal, for fraudulently obtaining £10,000 from a patient suffering from Alzheimer's in 2010. The tribunal determined that Mellotte's actions put patients at unnecessary risk, brought the profession into disrepute, and breached fundamental tenets of the profession, with her integrity being questionable.

A man, aged between 30 and 49, with Sikh symbol jewelry, was found near Shropshire's M54 motorway, dressed in clothing from around 2008. The investigation is ongoing, with no matches to missing persons, and police cannot rule out criminal activity. The remains are thought to have lain undiscovered for up to three years.

The surprise discovery in Avebury, a Neolithic site in England, reveals one of its earliest structures to be a "stone square circle" measureing 30m in size. This square of megaliths was found to enclose the obelisk and the remains of a house, thought to be the ancestral home of the first people who lived in Avebury. This finding is deemed unprecedented and may help explain why the Avebury monument complex was built.

Reading Borough Council's proposed parking scheme aimed at easing pressures around a hospital is faced with opposition from hospital staff, residents, and a local resident, who argue it will exacerbate parking issues, be particularly problematic for hospital staff and patients, and potentiallymake living in the area difficult. The council, however, claims it has consulted with the public for up to five years on prioritizing parking for residents. Residents have until 13 June to submit their views on the matter to the council.

U.S. Navy Petty Officer Aimee Mejia, 21, was involved in a three-car accident on Okinawa Island, injuring two people and driving with alcohol levels about six times the legal limit. As a result, the U.S. Navy has imposed stricter policies on personnel in Okinawa, where there is ongoing local opposition to the military presence, following a series of incidents.

In a highly successful tri-series, the Lions, coached by former England captain and coach, Duncan Fletcher, posted the second highest total in List A games with a 367-run partnership thanks to Sam Billings' 175, Duckett's ninth-highest List A score ever of 220 not out, and Bell-Drummond's 171. The team also defeated Sri Lanka A twice and Pakistan A on two occasions, with Dawid Malan scoring 185 and Duckett 163 not out in separate matches. Fletcher is optimistic that these performances may earn the young players international spots.

Colombia's peace talks with the FARC rebels are set to resume in Havana from December 10, aiming to de-escalate the conflict and address victim-family concerns, after the release of three hostages who were kidnapped in November. The five-decade-long conflict has allegedly resulted in over 220,000 deaths. The FARC had controversially kidnapped a general to express displeasure over ongoing military operations during peace negotiations, which the government continues to oppose, disputing that a truce would benefit the rebels.

The Save Oxfordshire Children's Centres Campaign, led by Jill Huish, held a protest against Oxfordshire County Council's plan to close 44 children's centers to save £8m, with more than 500 people participating. The protestors invited former Prime Minister David Cameron to join them, who had previously expressed disappointment about the cuts. The council maintains it will support the most vulnerable families while replacing the centers with eight "children and family centers" in needy areas. The government is encouraging local councils to make savings by consolidating back-office operations, disposing of surplus property, and joining public services.

A sandcastle depicting a dead murder victim and sexualized police officers in a sandcastle competition at a family beach event provoked criticism from a local council member as being offensive, insensitive, and trivializing serious matters, particularly the reporting of sex crimes, while some viewers defended it as a humorous representation of police work.

The new owner of Leyton Orient has taken control of the club, and manager Slade emphasizes that they are still working out the precise structure of the organization, aiming to improve and hopefully move up the league with potential new signings.

Tom Hatton, a 24-year-old golfer from Buckinghamshire, secured a spot at The Open Championship, USPGA at Baltusrol, and achieved his best European Tour finish of outright second with a prize payday of 429,468 euros. Despite missing chances on the back nine, Hatton stayed positive and showed impressive nerve, particularly making a crucial putt on the final green for a £150,000 difference in prize money. His goal for The Open is to make it through the weekend.

The 10-year-old Irish-bred horse, Many Clouds, succumbed to a rare case of severe pulmonary haemorrhage after narrowly winning the Cotswold Chase at Cheltenham's Festival Trials Day, despite having no significant underlying health issues. The British Horseracing Authority is determined to investigate further to better understand what causes these symptoms and potentially prevent them in the future.

The12-year-old witness testified in Sheffield Crown Court that she was taken out for a meal by Basharat Hussain and several other Asian males and then abused, also stating she was later forced to work in a Blackpool restaurant, sexually exploited, and infected with STDs. Basharat Hussain, along with six others, is on trial for child abuse in Rotherham, including charges such as rape and conspiracy to rape. The witness contradicted the defense lawyer's claim that she never met Basharat Hussain. The trial continues.

A 32-year-old racing cyclist, Franck Petricola, sadly passed away in an accident during the practice week of the TT race in the Isle of Man, making him the 141st fatality at the races since their inception in 1907. Despite suffering a severe accident the previous year at the North West 200, Petricola demonstrated resilience and determination by participating in this year's event. The event organizers offer their condolences to Petricola's family and friends.

Despite a much-anticipated return of Guy Martin to the Isle of Man TT following a crash in June and mechanical issues faced by his Honda Racing team this year, the racer will not participate due to the difficulties faced by the team; the event is expected to see impressive performances from Peter Hickman, Michael Dunlop, Dean Harrison, and potential dark horses.

President Barack Obama has declared Louisiana a disaster area due to devastating floods, which have left over 20,000 people rescued and thousands more still stranded in their homes. The floods, caused by torrential rain, have caused severe damage in the Louisiana capital Baton Rouge, with several rivers overflowing and many homes flooded up to three or four feet high. Emergency shelters are housing between 8,000 and 10,000 displaced people, as the flood is described as "unprecedented" and "of epic proportions" by local officials.

The concussion lawsuit against the federation by parents has been resolved, with US Soccer introducing new safety measures, including limiting the amount of heading for children aged 11 to 13, and making modifications to substitution rules for concussions, according to US Soccer's medical committee. Similar changes may be considered in England by the Football Association, who will soon announce guidelines for managing head injuries and researching long-term effects of head injuries on the brain.

Former presidential campaign deputy director Jerome Lavrilleux stated that Nicholas Sarkozy, Jean-Francois Cope (UMP Chairman), and Batien Millot (founder of Bygmalion) were unaware of almost 11 million euros worth of fake invoices to cover campaign overspends, which could damage the UMP party and complicate Sarkozy's potential re-election efforts. Patrick Maisonneuve, Bygmalion's lawyer, claims the UMP ordered the fake invoices, and the UMP's poor results in the European Parliament elections and speculation about Cope stepping down may further challenge Cope's leadership position.

The Council of Mortgage Lenders reported a decrease in home repossessions (2,500) from April to June 2021, compared to the previous quarter and the same quarter last year, due to low interest rates. However, they urge homeowners to prepare for future interest rate increases. Additionally, a fall in the number of homeowners in arrears was observed, but the number of tenants evicted by landlords increased, with Shelter attributing this to rising rents and welfare cuts.

The city of Coventry accepted 105 Syrian refugees over a six-month period, part of the UK's expanded resettlement programme for Syrian refugees, while other areas like Mid Sussex accepted fewer. UKIP MEP James Carver criticized the uneven distribution of refugees as unfair to Coventry, arguing it puts excessive pressure on the city's services. The Home Office expressed gratitude for the support of local authorities and aims to resettle 20,000 Syrian refugees by 2020 at a cost of £500m.

Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff, amid an economic crisis and concerns over security and pollution, promises that the upcoming 2016 Olympics in Rio will bring honor and pride to the country, with the torch relay starting in May 2016 in Brasilia, passing through 300 cities, and culminating at the Maracana stadium during the opening ceremony. She assures that the event will be safe, secure, and successful, and appeals to football World Cup fans to attend the Olympics. Despite challenges with delays in construction and pollution in Guanabara Bay, she expresses confidence in the country's ability to meet the challenges and deliver a historic Olympics.

Italian Prime Minister Matteo Renzi's legislative package, which received final approval in the lower house of parliament, includes a reform ensuring a majority of seats to the party winning the most votes in elections. The measure aims to mitigate Italy's post-war era of unstable governments by establishing a system that awards 340 out of 630 seats to parties securing more than 40% of the national vote and triggers a second-round run-off if no party meets the threshold. Opposition parties criticized the reform for giving too much power to single parties and denying voters direct representation, while the legislation's backers, including Mr. Renzi, contend it is necessary to bring political stability to the country. Renzi also intends to abolish the Senate and replace it with a body with lesser powers.

The 20-year-old football player Abdelhak Nouri, while playing for Ajax against Werder Bremen, experienced cardiac arrhythmias, and post-evaluation suggests he is unlikely to recover due to brain damage caused by a lack of oxygen supply.

Swansea, having lost six straight games, secured an important victory at Villa Park, with Andre Ayew scoring a late winner after Jordan Ayew had started the scoring for Villa, and Gylfi Sigurdsson crediting the team's character and improved performance for the win. The loss marked the end of Tim Sherwood's managerial tenure at Villa, while the win lifts Swansea past Villa in the table and gives them confidence for their upcoming home game against Arsenal.

A Polish mother named Leyla Dad, using the middle name Paulina, is searching for her son Mani Dad, believed to be in the UK with his British father Zayn Dean, and is pleading with Costa coffee shop employees and customers to help find him, as he frequently visited these establishans when the family lived in England. The family had previously resided in Kettering, Northamptonshire, and Bedford before moving to Poland. Leyla launched family court proceedings to locate her son and has asked anyone with information to contact the authorities.

Dual citizens of Iran, Iraq, Syria, and Sudan, including a BBC presenter, are facing travel restrictions to the US under new visa rules, which they deem unfair due to ambiguity in implementation advice and potential impact on families. The rules were implemented following heightened security concerns post Paris attacks, but European ambassadors have expressed concerns about disproportionate and unfair impact on dual nationals.

Sky is working to increase capacity at telephone exchanges in areas where it's facing network strain, particularly in Doncaster, North Wales, and Bristol, due to a rise in network traffic and new customer additions. This issue has been affecting fewer than 5% of its broadband customers, and has been exacerbated by the launch of Sky Go Extra, which allows offline streaming, potentially straining the network further. The issue comes as Sky has run a promotion highlighting unlimited data usage, possibly attracting customers who consume significantly more data than average.

A gang consisting of Joseph McHale, Kevin Schruyers, and Robin Vaughan from Liverpool was convicted for targeting ATMs across various Scottish locations from August to November 2013, using explosives; they stole substantial amounts from cash machines in Aberdeen, New Deer, and Ellon, as well as attempted break-ins and stealing from a golf shop. A Scottish resident, Francis Clark, played a role in providing them a hideaway, initially leading to his initial suspicion but later serving as a witness in the trial. Sentencing has been deferred to next month at the High Court at Livingston. Police Scotland acknowledged the complex investigation and the public's assistance as crucial.

Scottish Prison Service, under MacAskill's leadership, is set to implement new technology to disrupt mobile phone signals at two pilot prisons (HMP Shotts and Glenochil) following legislation approval, aiming to address the ongoing issues of contraband phone usage linked to drug supply, organized crime, and harassment in prisons.

French former President Francois Hollande attended a ceremony at a former Nazi camp in Alsace to commemorate the 70th anniversary of its liberation, where he highlighted the importance of knowledge as a means of preventing future atrocities, while the ongoing surge of attacks on Jews and Muslims in France has reignited debate about social tensions, as acknowledged by BBC's Lucy Williamson. Parallel ceremonies were held in Germany for the liberation of Bergen-Belsen, where Anne Frank perished, and in Croatia for the escape attempt from Jasenovac. Remarks were made by figures such as Ronald Lauder, President of the World Jewish Congress, who recollected the initial horrific images from Bergen-Belsen, and attended by approximately 70 survivors of various camps.

Actor Johnny Depp, 52, and his wife Amber Heard, 30, are divorcing due to irreconcilable differences, with Heard filing in Los Angeles Superior Court. Recent legal issues arose when Heard illegally brought two dogs into Australia, leading to a months-long feud with Australia's Deputy PM Barnaby Joyce. The divorce coincides with Depp's mother's death and the release of his latest film, Alice Through the Looking Glass.

A container ship, Maersk Tigris, with a multinational crew, remains anchored off Bandar Abbas, allegedly seized by Iranian authorities due to a court order related to a debt claim by a private Iranian company. The ship was in international shipping lanes, with no U.S. nationals among the crew. Maersk is seeking more information about the seizure, while the U.S. Navy has dispatched a destroyer and a reconnaissance plane to the area. The ship was initially ordered deeper into Iranian waters by Iranian Revolutionary Guards Navy patrol vessels, who subsequently fired warning shots and forced the ship to comply. The U.S. Navy described these actions as "inappropriate".

A request to disclose the full investigation report on a 14-year-old girl's suicide in 2012 was denied by Pembrokeshire council due to legal advice, leaving the girl's mother feeling traumatized due to unanswered questions, despite the report being deemed a document for learning.

In a pivotal Super League match, Leigh secured a decisive 18-0 victory over Salford, ensuring Widnes Vikings would finish at the bottom of the league at the end of the regular season. Leigh's win, marked by strong performances from Gregg McNally, Samisoni Langi, and Josh Drinkwater, boosted their morale and positioned them positively as the Super 8 qualifiers approach. Salford, on the other hand, fell to a fifth consecutive defeat, failing to secure third place and dropping to fourth due to results from other games. Salford's coach, Ian Watson, acknowledged a dip in their performances and the need to reignite their early-season intensity.

Paul Allen, aided by Burt Rutan and Elon Musk, is developing a giant aircraft, Stratolaunch Systems, to put unmanned rockets into orbit from high-flying aircraft, with plans for manned missions later. The aircraft, slated for test flights in 2016, will have a 385ft wingspan wider than the Spruce Goose, and is designed to save on rocket fuel and offer launch flexibility, while also serving the commercial satellite industry and the International Space Station.

Despite Lancashire establishing a significant 264-run lead in the match thanks to Alex Davies' impressive 89, Derbyshire manage to dismiss their openers Ben Slater and Billy Godleman, leaving them on 27-2, with the possibility of winning the match dependent on substantial partnerships and individual contributions.

Jon Stewart, known for his influence as a satirist and liberal voice in America on The Daily Show, hosted a final show with guest appearances from Bruce Springsteen, John Kerry, and John McCain, with several well-known comic performers also acknowledged for their start on the show. The show served as an emotional farewell, with Stewart expressing gratitude towards colleagues, fans, and family, before a humorous departure by saying he'll go get a drink, and the show's hashtag #JonVoyage trending on Twitter.

Forest, a four-time cup winner looking to compete again at the Europa League level, will attempt to progress past the third round for the first time in 11 seasons when they visit Doncaster, following their opening victory in the Championship against Burton Albion.

The Arches nightclub has gone into administration following a midnight closure ruling due to drug abuse and disorder concerns, potentially affecting 130 jobs. The Scottish Government, Creative Scotland, Glasgow City Council, and the Arches management have been urged to collaborate to find a solution to either reverse or expedite the reopening of the cultural venue in Glasgow. The government has pledged support to affected staff through the Partnership Action for Continuing Employment (PACE) initiative.

A 77-year-old, Ivor Bell, a former senior Provisional IRA leader, was arrested in connection with aiding and abetting murder and membership of the IRA, particularly in relation to the disappearance and death of Jean McConville in 1972, who was later recognized as one of the "Disappeared" during the Troubles. McConville was a mother of 10 who was accused of being an informer before her murder, and her body was recovered in 2003. The IRA admitted in 1999 to murdering and secretly burying nine of the Disappeared, and despite extensive searches, the remains of seven of them have not been found.

Wigan Warriors overcame a 12-man disadvantage following a red card to Ben Flower and scored 21 unanswered points to secure victory against Catalans Dragons, boosting their confidence for the rest of the season. Despite the League Leaders' Shield being in Warrington's grasp, Wigan are still aiming for a home semi-final and a fourth consecutive final appearance.

The Yorkshire Sculpture Park experienced a 170% increase in visitor numbers in September, with 100,000 people visiting to see the poppy installation; expecting its highest visitor numbers ever, with more than half a million visitors. The poppy installation, Wave, consisting of 5,800 ceramic poppies, is part of a nationwide tour commemorating the 100th anniversary of World War One and has attracted a significant number of visitors.

A severe flood warning on the A361 road between East Lyng and Burrowbridge was lifted on 10 March, after which temporary traffic lights were installed. This was due to water remaining on a short stretch of the road. The reopening was hailed as a relief by Councillor Harvey Siggs, who thanked his team for their hard work. The council will review the road again next week, after which the traffic lights will be removed. The A372 Langport Road remains closed for the removal of flood pumps, and improving weather has led to the removal of large temporary pumps at Beer Wall, near Aller.

A newly discovered object, V774104, observed by Japan's Subaru telescope, is estimated to be approximately 500-1,000 km across and currently about three times further from the Sun than Pluto, making it the most distant known object. its trajectory pattern is yet unclear as scientists are observing it to understand its orbit and behavior within the Solar System.

Ashley Yates, a former headteacher at The Tynings Primary School, admitted to making indecent images of children and voyeurism, recording images of pupils and staff, including additional adult victims, using a spy pen. He has been remanded in custody for further court hearings. The school is cooperating with police and local authorities, offering support to identified victims and providing information without compromising the legal proceedings.

Great Britain's rowing team, consisting of Helena Glover and Heather Stanning, dominated the Women's Pair event at the Rio Olympics, winning gold with a time of 7 minutes 18.29 seconds, 1.2 seconds ahead of New Zealand. Their victory marks their 17th Olympic medal for Britain, moving them up to fourth place in the overall standings. This is their second gold in this event, having previously won in 2012, and the pair are now unbeaten in 39 races, a streak that spans five years. The win is particularly significant for the athletes, who say it means much more than their London Games victory due to the pressure of defending a title. The crowd and media, including former Olympian Sir Steve Redgrave and singer Pixie Lott, praised the women's impressive performance.

Steve and Ola, participants on Strictly Come Dancing, have faced unfounded bullying allegations and have chosen to respond by presenting a united front, continuing to dance and ignoring the claims, with Steve stating that it's been their biggest learning experience on the show and that they've answered the allegations truthfully.

The article reports that inflation dropped to 2.6% in June from 2.9%, leading to a decline in the value of the pound against both the U.S. dollar and the euro. The drop in inflation lowered expectations for an immediate interest rate hike, but it may not completely rule out one happening this year if conditions improve. The fall in the pound initially lifted the FTSE 100 index, but it closed down 13.91, while Royal Mail shares rose following a 1% increase in revenues.

Actress Vicky McClure, who has a tram in Nottingham named after her, experienced a misunderstanding in 2015 when a conductor asked for her ticket, despite her and her mother being offered a free ride after the tram was named in her honor.

The inquest into the death of 14-year-old Alice Gross, who was found dead in the River Brent in west London in September 2014, will examine if government and police failures contributed to her death and whether the systems for monitoring foreign offenders are robust. Alice's mother, Rosalind Hodgkiss, expressed concerns about the lack of monitoring of foreign national Arnis Zalkalns, a convicted murderer who was the prime suspect in Alice's death but died before being charged. Zalkalns was also the suspect in his own wife's murder.

The Local Data Company and the University of Stirling's research shows that Scotland's average retail vacancy rate decreased from 14.5% to 13.7%, with East Kilbride having the highest vacancy rate and Inverurie the lowest. Nearly 40% of empty stores have been vacant for more than three years, and town vacancy rates improved at twice the rate of cities. The report highlights the growing significance of leisure businesses in towns and cities, with Aberdeen having the highest proportion of charity shops in a city, and Penicuik in Midlothian having the greatest proportion of charity shops in a town. Matthew Hopkinson of the Local Data Company notes the chronic vacancy issue, particularly in towns, implying obsolescence and a barrier to healthy communities.

Rory McWhirter fraudulently obtained personal details from individuals for fake job applications, securing their marriage certificates to falsely register births, and ultimately claimed benefits amounting to over £34,000 in Scotland's Dundee Sheriff Court. His scheme was exposed when he was recognized at an Aberdeen registry office where he had previously registered a false birth.

The authorities are attempting to demolish Awamiya's old quarter, a predominantly Shia area in Eastern Province, with clashes resulting in several deaths, according to reports. Activists claim forces are indiscriminately firing towards homes, causing damage, and forced displacement, while residents complain of marginalization, discrimination, and lack of essential services. The unrest has persisted since the 2011 Arab Spring and escalated following the 2016 execution of Shia cleric Nimr al-Nimr, a supporter of the protests.

The article discusses the frustrations of young people in Belfast, aged 16 to 18, who are struggling to find employment despite having completed their education. They express disappointment at not receiving job offers despite numerous applications, and are critical of politicians for being more focused on elections than addressing the needs of the youth, including job training, drug reform, and improving healthcare. The young interviewees also feel that politicians should be more accessible and visible during non-election periods.

Barnet Council's Chief Executive, Andrew Travers, has departed the council following a fiasco where election voters were turned away due to their names being missing from the poll list; an independent investigation is underway to assess the appropriateness of election arrangements, including the EU Referendum in June.

Manager Neil Warnock has given midfielder Peter Whittingham ample time to consider a new contract offer, while finding alternative entrées for Emyr Huws and Stuart O'Keefe who are not part of his long-term plans.

A BBC and BuzzFeed News investigation has unearthed suspected match-fixing allegations in elite tennis, with tennis representative Fleming emphasizing the importance of maintaining the integrity and purity of the sport, stating that if culprits are found, they should be banned, and suggesting additional funding for the Tennis Integrity Unit to combat this issue.

A 60-year-old man, suspected of producing a firearm but without making threats or demands, surrendered to police after holding a female staff member hostage in a bank interview room in Northfield, Birmingham. The incident resulted in a heavy police response, including armed officers, but no customers were harmed. The suspect was taken to hospital for an assessment and is expected to be questioned for firearms offenses.

A Liverpool man, Mohammed Ali, alleged to have used the dark net under the alias "Weirdos 0000" to attempt to purchase a lethal dose of ricin, a chemical toxin, denies charges at the Old Bailey. The court heard that Ali, a computer software programmer who displays traits of Asperger's syndrome, was motivated by watching the series Breaking Bad and was arrested after taking delivery of a toy car containing harmless powder instead of the ricin.

Newport County is facing criticism over the condition of Rodney Parade's pitch, with Chief Executive of Rodney Parade Limited, Davies, stating that the cost of maintenance exceeds the revenue received from the football club's seasonal lease.

Approximately 69% of the surveyed individuals admitted to working while unwell, primarily due to fear of accumulating work, while 23% falsely claimed sick days. The report suggests this "presenteeism" culture, driven by increased work demands, negatively affects productivity and morale in the workplace.

The British pound declined against both the US dollar and the euro, while the Bank of England kept its key interest rate at 0.25%, prompting some anticipation for a potential rate rise. Stocks remained fairly stable, with the FTSE 100 almost flat, but key movers included silver miner Fresnillo with a 5% increase, Hikma plunging due to US regulatory challenges, Centrica's continued decline, and BT's dip following a slide in annual profits.

Russian hacker, the son of a Russian MP, was found guilty of running a scheme targeting US pizza chains in Washington state from 2008 to 2014, stealing nearly 3 million credit card numbers, and facing a four-year mandatory jail term after being convicted on 38 out of 40 charges. The legal team plans to appeal, citing the illegal arrest and evidence usage in the case, with claims of political involvement. Russia has lodged complaints about Seleznev's seizure and extradition.

The individual stated that he does not possess any recordings as insinuated by a previous tweet regarding a conversation with former FBI Director James Comey, who earlier confirmed under oath that the president asked him to drop an investigation and gave assurances of loyalty. Recent news reports have suggested that during a private meeting, the president may have inquired about exonerating his former National Security Adviser regarding lying to federal agents about a conversation with the Russian ambassador. This has led to speculation and pressure for the president to produce any potentially existing recordings amid ongoing inquiries into alleged Russian meddling in the 2016 election.

Liberty, led by Sanjeev Gupta, is the first to express interest in purchasing Tata Steel's UK assets, with a bid expected to be submitted on Tuesday. The firm, known for focusing on recycling scrap metal rather than traditional steel production, has already acquired several steel plants in the UK in recent years. Other potential bidders include a management buyout team, Excalibur Steel UK Limited. Tata Steel is under pressure to sell due to ongoing losses and cannot sustain them indefinitely.

The 19 councils in the Nottingham region are prioritizing the proposal for a tram system that would connect East Midlands Airport, the proposed HS2 station at Toton, Derby, and Nottingham in their devolution negotiations, with a possible cost of £200m for the route from Toton to Derby, and no specific timetable mentioned. This is one of several strategic transport projects aimed at maximizing the region's growth potential.

The five-time world champion, media-named snooker player Ronnie O'Sullivan, has won the Masters 2021 with a 10-1 victory over Barry Hawkins. Despite recent health issues and a brief absence from the game, O'Sullivan attributes his win to modifying his game style to keep up with the younger generation. He believes this adjustment, including adding more power to his shots, will aid him in future competitions, including the World Championship in April.

The devastating weekend storms in Poland resulted in six fatalities, extensive property damage, and the felling of over eight million cubic meters of lumber across 45,000 hectares of forest, particularly affecting areas like Torun, Gdansk, and Poznan. The incident is said to be the worst forest disaster in Polish (and possibly European) history. The disaster occurs amid ongoing criticism of the Polish government's logging activities in the Bialowieza forest, a Unesco world heritage site and home to rare wildlife, with future legal actions possible by the EU.

Singer Enrique Iglesias was injured at a concert in Tijuana, Mexico when he reached for a drone camera taking photos of the audience, requiring reconstructive surgery and subsequent recovery for several weeks before resuming his tour on July 3 in Mexico City.

In the Super League match between Leeds Rhinos and Warrington Wolves, Matt Parcell scored a hat-trick, Joel Moon scored his 15th try in 16 games, and Jamie Jones-Buchanan also scored as Leeds Rhinos beat Warrington Wolves 26-0, keeping the Wire scoreless. Leeds moved up to third place with their fifth win in seven games.

William (Plum) Smith, who spent a decade in prison for a 1972 shooting and played a crucial role in the 1994 ceasefire of loyalist paramilitary groups, was remembered for his significant contributions to peace efforts and his negotiations with paramilitary groups, as well as his education and support for the Irish language. He was a respected figure in the Progressive Unionist Party and the loyalist community, notably for his left-of-center politics and his dedication to the working class.

Olive Cooke, a 92-year-old Bristol resident, has faithfully sold poppies for the Royal British Legion for over 75 years, having joined at age 16 following her father. Her dedication intensified after the loss of her first husband in World War II, and she continues to sell poppies annually at Bristol Cathedral. The Legion recognizes her as a profoundly valued and well-loved member of their volunteer team.

Shimon Peres, a prominent Israeli statesman and peace activist, former Prime Minister and President, who played a crucial role in Israel's founding and peace negotiations with the Palestinians, winning the Nobel Peace Prize in 1994; died following a stroke two weeks prior, with expressions of grief from various world leaders.

The BBC reports that a major survey conducted at Queen's University revealed suboptimal perceptions of senior leadership and change management, with only 29% of respondents expressing satisfaction. However, the survey also highlighted at least 89% of staff found their work interesting, two-thirds felt proud to work there, and nearly nine in ten considered the university highly respected in Northern Ireland. The university acknowledged the results, emphasizing commitment to staff engagement, improving work environment, and actively addressing areas identified as challenges.

The X-47B jet, a tailless, stealthy unmanned aircraft developed by Northrop Grumman for the US Navy, successfully completed its maiden flight, marking a significant step towards a new era of unmanned drone technology, with plans for testing on aircraft carriers in 2013.

Airbus has reduced the planned deliveries of its double-decker A380 planes due to low sales prospects, while continuing production at a marginal loss. The company also anticipates continued reliability issues with one of the engines for the A320neo aircraft from Pratt & Whitney, and is in talks with Qatar Airways to address a recent cancellation of four A350 aircraft. Meanwhile, Airbus' Q2 profits fell considerably compared to analyst expectations, while Boeing saw record highs in profits and shares.

The article reports that 40% of coral has died at Dongsha Atoll in the South China Sea, a significant loss not observed in the past 40 years, primarily due to the devastating 2015/2016 El Niño affecting reefs globally, including Dongsha. While a 2-degree cap on ocean warming may be insufficient to save coral reefs in general, local weather variations can raise temperatures to lethal levels for shallow water reefs like Dongsha. To preserve coral reefs, experts urge drastic action to reduce global warming.

Researchers at the University of Queensland and Monash University have discovered a protein found in the venom of Australian funnel-web spiders named Hi1a, which has shown significant potential as a future stroke treatment by blocking acid-sensing ion channels in the brain and minimizing brain damage after a stroke. However, the research is still in its early stages and has not yet been tested on humans. The Stroke Association welcomes this development and emphasizes the need for more research and human trials.

A thrilling Football League match between Oldham Athletic and Bradford City ended 1-1. Oldham took an early lead through Peter Clarke's header, but Bradford dominated the rest of the first half. The visitors managed to hold on to their lead until the 57th minute when they were penalized for a foul in the box, and Bradford's Billy Clarke scored from the spot. Both teams had numerous opportunities throughout the game, but could not find a winning goal. In the second half, Oldham's Connor Ripley made a remarkable save to keep his team in the game, and Bradford's Billy Clarke converted a penalty to level the score at 1-1.

The article reports that a drug called aducanumab, which targets the build-up of amyloid in the brain, has shown initial promise in a small study for slowing memory decline in patients with Alzheimer's disease, but experts are cautious due to its early stage of development, potential side effects, and the lengthy phase 3 clinical trials underway to fully evaluate its effects.

Lowly Oldham Roughyeds pulled off a stunning upset in the Challenge Cup, defeating Hull KR 24-34, despite the latter finishing with 12 men. This was Oldham's biggest win since the club reformed in 1997, and Hull KR coach James Webster described his team's performance as an "utter embarrassment". On the other hand, the Roughyeds coach was delighted with the victory, referring to it as a "massive day" for the club.

The BBC's director general, Tony Hall, has outlined a strategy for the corporation's future, aiming to become an "open BBC for the internet age," with plans for a children's iPlayer, a pool of local reporters, and an Ideas Service collaborating with cultural institutions. However, he also warned of necessary funding cuts leading to the reduction or loss of some services, and the closing of others, without specifying affected areas. The BBC's plans have faced criticism from the newspaper industry over perceived encroachment into local news provision.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission has written to political leaders expressing concern over an increase in hate attacks since the UK's EU referendum, including the killing of Arkadiusz Jozwick and anti-Semitic, homophobic, and racist incidents. They call for accurate information and respectful debate from politicians, and urge them to consider the impact of their words and policies on society. The commission also criticizes the government's aborted plan to demand companies disclose the proportion of foreign workers they employ, and suggests a review of sentences for hate crimes.

Ms. Evans, formerly a UKIP policy maker and the author of their 2015 general election manifesto, expressed her desire to run for leader but said a small group of party higher-ups have ensured her exclusion due to a six-month ban for bringing the party into disrepute. She endorsed Lisa Duffy, a district councillor, as the best candidate to lead UKIP and change the party's image, aiming for a "clean break from the past" and a more unified, consensual direction.

In England, a new grading system will replace traditional letters with numbers (1-9), and coursework will be eliminated for most subjects starting with students taking GCSEs in 2017. The changes in curriculum and assessment format are intended to improve core skills in maths and English, with a focus on deep learning, grammar, spelling, and punctuation. The reforms are facing mixed reactions from educational institutions and unions, with concerns about potential negative impacts on less able students.

Retired Gen. David Petraeus, who served under Presidents Bush and Obama and faced a scandal regarding classified material, indicated a willingness to serve under Trump if asked and suggested that Trump's potential outreach to Russia could be comparable to Nixon's overtures to China.

The article describes a stand-off between supporters of Egypt's newly elected President Mohammed Mursi and the military, which has been ruling since Hosni Mubarak was ousted last year. During a meeting with President Mursi, Hillary Clinton emphasized the need for compromise and real politics, while acknowledging the role of the military council in Egypt's interim leadership. The US is cautiously engaging with President Mursi's government, as it is important for the US and Egypt to work together. The article also mentions ongoing protests against Mursi's government and concerns about the parliament, as well as Clinton's plans to address the head of the Supreme Council of the Armed Forces and discuss the return of the armed forces to a purely military role.

The article discusses Derek Bruder's testimony in the inquests focusing on the final movements of 15-year-old Kevin Williams during the 1989 FA Cup semi-final disaster. Bruder recalled a meeting with former Insp Matthew Sawers, who was accused of attempting to change Bruder's statement regarding Kevin's vital signs. Bruder asserted that Sawers had pressure him to alter his statement, while Sawers denied this allegation. The investigation continues, with the inquests resuming next Monday.

Oh Wonder, a band consisting of Josephine and Anthony West, went incognito for a year while their music gained popularity on Soundcloud, creating a mysterious but dedicated fanbase. This period also included an anecdote where Josephine struck up a conversation with a bloodied stranger on a train, leading to a song titled "High on Humans." The new album, Ultralife, is instrumental in embodying the band's experiences of human connection and the joys and challenges that come with popularity. Despite the potential risk of losing their anonymity, the duo values the authentic interactions they can have on public transportation.

In a Premier League clash, Chelsea's Bertrand Traore capitalized on a pass from Nemanja Matic to give his team the lead against Stoke City. The Potters responded through Diouf after a cross by Xherdan Shaqiri was poorly dealt with by Courtois, as the match ended 1-1. Both teams remain in mid-table positions, with Stoke in 7th and Chelsea in 10th.

The research conducted by William C Campbell, Satoshi Omura, and Youyou Tu led to the discovery of life-changing drugs (ivermectin, artemisinin) that combat diseases like malaria, river blindness (onchocerciasis), and elephantiasis (lympatic filariasis), affecting over 3.4 billion people globally. These treatments are particularly significant as they target lesser-known parasitic illnesses. Ivermectin was derived from a Japanese soil bacterium discovered by Omura, while artemisinin was deduced from the sweet wormwood plant by Youyou Tu.

The article discusses the Nelson Mandela Foundation's criticism of South African President Zuma for allegedly allowing corruption and misuse of state resources, and the Friends of Nelson Mandela's call for accountability. The Foundation considered South Africa's democracy to be under threat, as key institutions were allegedly being used for personal gain. They pointed towards the Gupta family as an example of private interests undermining state institutions. The Foundation also highlighted that Mr. Zuma's leadership had failed the test of leadership.

Comedian and actress Miranda did a gallop during the curtain call at the opening night of Annie, a West End musical, where she played the "big and brash and clowny" Miss Hannigan, with generally positive reviews (four stars from The Telegraph, three stars from The Guardian) for her performance that's described as a balance between menace and humor. The show features 12-year-old Ruby Stokes, amongst others, as the main character Annie, alongside her dog Sandy. The optimism of the show is seen as particularly relevant in light of recent terror attacks in London.

In this article, it is reported that Georginio Wijnaldum scored two goals, one each assisted by Shelvey, as Newcastle United managed a 2-1 win over West Ham United, moving them out of the relegation zone. A stray backpass by Chancel Mbemba allowed Nikica Jelavic to score for the visitors, but Newcastle held on despite missing several chances. The team's new signing, Shelvey, produced a good performance, as did striker Aleksandar Mitrovic who was denied three times by the Hammers' keeper, Adrian. The win was a welcome one for manager Steve McClaren, who had previously lost to West Ham this season.

Major supermarkets in the UK broke tradition by reducing diesel prices below petrol, with Morrisons initiating the move due to lower wholesale costs. Previously, diesel prices had been consistently higher, according to the UK Petroleum Industry Association, due to a decrease in petrol demand following increased engine efficiency. Experts predict that diesel prices could further drop by up to 4p per litre, with petrol potentially experiencing slight reductions as well. The shift is attributed mainly to an increased diesel supply from refineries outside the UK.

The UN General Assembly's 70th gathering underlined the continual challenges facing Africa, including wars, coups, poverty, hunger, and refugee crises, while also providing crucial support and peacekeeping missions. A major concern remains ending hunger, with many countries in southern Africa currently facing food crises, and the new Sustainable Development Goals being met with hope to address these issues.

Superman-branded pills containing the dangerous chemical PMMA, known for causing overdoses due to its slow acting nature, may still be circulating, warns the police, with Dr Adam Winstock suggesting that such drugs could be unintentionally packaged as MDMA tablets, and cannot be identified through home testing kits. The public is cautioned to prioritize safety, keep well-hydrated, monitor friends for symptoms, and seek medical help if concerned.

In a letter to UKIP leader Paul Nuttall, Leave.EU campaign chairman Mr Banks suggested that ex-leader Nigel Farage should return to the party and that he, Mr Banks, should become chair to transform UKIP into a viable, efficient political force.

This article describes a service called Invisible Girlfriend/Boyfriend that allows users to create a virtual romantic partner and pay for text messages, voicemails, and other interactions to give the impression of a real relationship. The service, while initially seeming ludicrous and pathetic, has attracted thousands of users, with about 60% choosing boyfriends, for various reasons including getting parents off their backs, avoiding unwanted attention, and practicing flirting.

Germany displayed a dominant offensive performance in a 2-0 victory over Poland, with Thomas Muller, Karim Bellarabi, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and Mario Gotze standout contributors. However, they showed minor vulnerabilities in defence, which Scotland may exploit in their upcoming match.

In the championship, an equalizer by Sam Gallagher in the final moments denied Bristol City a third successive win as they remain four points above the relegation zone, while Rovers are still two points from safety, with three games remaining; both teams missed chances throughout the game, with on-loan Chelsea striker Tammy Abraham having the best opportunity but striking straight at the goalkeeper.

Scotland aims to send off outgoing coach Gregor Townsend's successor, Vern Cotter, with a victory over Ireland in the opening Six Nations match, despite Ireland's significant advantage in previous championship encounters. The Scottish team, boosted by the motivation of wanting to offer a fitting farewell, will feature Ryan Wilson at number eight. Ireland's Joe Schmidt is expected to exploit Scotland's weaknesses, particularly in the set-piece battle, as his inexperienced Scottish front-row faces a stern test.

John Guidetti scores a free-kick following Pascali's red card and a professional foul on Scepovic, Kilmarnock's goalkeeper Conor Brennan makes several impressive saves but Scepovic scores a second goal after the break, ultimately securing a 2-0 victory for Celtic in the Scottish Premiership.

According to a study by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), Northern Irish pupils have higher life satisfaction scores compared to their counterparts in the UK, yet concerns over exam anxiety, bullying, and heavy internet usage remain issues. Northern Irish pupils have high levels of academic ambition and strong relationships with parents and teachers, which positively influence their academic performance and life satisfaction. However, extensive internet use has been linked to a decrease in life satisfaction. The study reveals significant variations in life satisfaction across the 72 OECD countries, with low rates in South Korea and Turkey and higher rates in the Netherlands. In Northern Ireland, while life satisfaction scores are relatively high, 12.6% of pupils still report low levels of satisfaction. The study suggests that girls and disadvantaged students are less likely to report high levels of life satisfaction compared to boys and advantaged students.

Everton came from behind in a physical and tactically astute game against Crystal Palace, with Romelu Lukaku scoring and Leighton Baines converting a late penalty, but Palace held on for a 3-2 victory, building on their resilience and self-belief. Neil Warnock's side showed character after a slow start and proved too much for Everton to handle despite the latter's initial dominance.

Freelance sports journalist Gary Carter, aged 36, was found with head injuries in Bethnal Green early on Friday morning following an altercation. His wife Gemma stated that he was heavily sedated while waiting for the swelling on his brain to subside. A 35-year-old man, James Flanagan, was charged with causing grievous bodily harm. The case is currently under investigation by Scotland Yard. Carter, who regularly works for The Sun, was in London to cover a rugby league match between England and New Zealand. His colleagues in the sport and on social media have expressed well-wishes for a speedy recovery.

British rapper Tinie Tempah, who holds the record for the most number one singles in this decade amongst British artists, discusses his second home studio, where he has been working on his third album Youth for more than two years, having taken inspiration from meeting up with his friends to reignite his creativity and connect with his roots. He reflects on his journey from Peckham's Aylesbury estate to achieving success in the music industry, and he acknowledges the self-reliance of new generation artists like Skepta and Stormzy, celebrating the growing acceptance of British rap as a mainstream genre. The the album Youth is set for release on 14 April.

Mobile operators, led by O2, are hoping to expedite the allocation of spectrum by the communications regulator Ofcom, in order to launch 4G networks earlier than previously expected, potentially as early as May or June. EE, a rival network, may announce its 4G launch date as soon as this month, despite previously had gained an advantage due to an early approval to use its existing 1,800MHz spectrum for 4G service. The delay for other networks, such as O2 and Vodafone, is due to the ongoing negotiations for auctioning the necessary portions of the radio spectrum. The process could be sped up by a fortnight, but potential legal challenges may cause further delay. EE's early launch may have been advantageous, but a challenging task remains for EE to effectively market its 4G service and capitalize on the competition.

The Conservative party has decided to forgo a free lunch program for the youngest primary school children, citing cost concerns, and instead will offer only a free breakfast. Some teachers and educators are upset by this decision, as they feel it may exacerbate child hunger and undermine the positive impact that the free lunch program has had in some schools.

A shooting incident took place at a busy downtown area of Tel Aviv, leaving four seriously injured. Israeli security forces have launched a manhunt to find the gunman, whose identity and motive remain unclear, but speculation has emerged that it may be linked to organized crime or a hate crime. Meanwhile, previous violence in the region has left 21 Israelis and 131 Palestinians dead over the past few months.

A Scotland-based artist's research into his family tree, including his great great grandfather Ambrose Salvona who was a circus performer in Scotland and was believed to have arrived with a dancing bear in the late 19th Century, led a local resident to find Salvona's grave in Inverness' Tomnahurich Cemetery. This discovery influenced the writing of a song about his grandmother, Dora Salvona Owens, who grew up in the circus.

At Glastonbury 2021, sustainably-sourced recycled steel pint cups are introduced on a major scale for the first time. However, they are not compulsory and not all bars offer them. Their awkward shape and lack of a logo make them identifiable only to fellow festivalgoers. Despite being made from food-grade stainless steel, there are concerns about physically throwing them due to their lack of aerodynamics and weight. The festival organizers aim to promote the use of British steel, with the cups being manufactured in Birmingham after being sourced in Sheffield. The use of these cups is part of the "reusable revolution," similar to charging for plastic bags. However, the production of these steel cups also involves emissions, while plastic glasses release harmful toxins and remain in the environment for a long time due to their stability.

A 15-year-old boy survived the earthquake by drinking water from wet clothes and eating clarified butter, while a woman in her 20s was rescued after being trapped for over 8 hours. The rescue effort involves teams from various countries, but relief efforts are being hampered by bad weather and difficulties reaching remote areas. Many survivors are falling ill due to contaminated water, and the death toll has risen to 6,130 with over 13,000 injured. The UN estimates that over 8 million people have been affected and about 70,000 houses destroyed.

JP Morgan plans to relocate hundreds to potentially thousands of staff to Dublin, Frankfurt, and Luxembourg as part of contingency plans for Brexit, following similar announcements from various financial services companies regarding the movement of staff out of London.

In the suburb of Ferguson after the shooting of an unarmed black teenager, Michael Brown, by a white police officer, a crowd of around 150 clashed with police during a curfew, leading to multiple arrests, a police vehicle being targeted by gunfire, and allegations of police brutality. The US Justice Department is investigating, with 40 FBI agents dispatched to gather information. The officer who shot Brown, Darren Wilson, a six-year police veteran with no previous complaints, has been on administrative leave since the shooting. The incident has sparked violent protests and widespread outrage across the US and internationally, with nationwide vigils held and civil rights leader Al Sharpton planning a peaceful rally led by Brown's family.

Diane Abbott, the Labour shadow home secretary, criticized Theresa May for allowing a decrease in police officer numbers during May's tenure as home secretary, suggesting this contributed to the falling ability to keep the public safe, particularly in view of the recent London and Manchester terror attacks. Conservative Party officials, however, dismissed Abbott's claims as "dangerous" and cited an increase in armed police numbers, while also asserting that she had opposed various security-related legislative measures.

The world champions, New Zealand, routed Wales in the final Test with a score of 46-6, marking Wales' 29th consecutive loss to the All Blacks and the heaviest loss for Wales in nine years. Warren Gatland, the Welsh coach, sees numerous lessons for his team from this defeat, aiming to improve on these learnings when they meet again. Steve Hansen, the New Zealand coach, attributes Wales' performance to their long season, suggesting they will re-group and be stronger in the Six Nations.

Five individuals, including a 17-year-old British boy named Stephen Thomas who was a talented photographer and a driving force behind the Swindon Down's Syndrome Group, died in a boat accident in Canada. They were not wearing life jackets on the open, upper deck of the boat. The other passengers were in an enclosed part. The boat, operated by the same company as a previous incident in 1998, capsized unexpectedly. The cause of the accident is under investigation by Canadian government investigators. The amazing response from local residents around Tofino prevented more deaths, but a 27-year-old Australian man is still missing.

The article discusses President Thein Sein's statement that a ceasefire agreement in Myanmar marks a new road to future peace but only includes half of the armed groups, including the Karen National Union and some noteworthy ones like the United Wa State Army and the Kachin Independence Organisation that were not part of the deal. The government aims to continue efforts to bring these groups into the process for political discussions on a new, likely more federal system of government, with concerns for short-lived peace if the Burmese army fails to adhere to the ceasefire, as it has with others in the past.

Facebook was ordered to remove a page targeting a Northern Irish man with a history of sexual offenses from the 1980s, as it amounted to harassment and a potential violation of his human rights. The man sought an interim injunction and damages from Facebook Ireland Ltd, citing threats to his safety. While the ruling allows the man's name, criminal record, and whereabouts to remain public, it requires Facebook to take steps to prevent further alleged unlawful conduct against the man. The judge acknowledged that such cases are highly fact-specific and do not extend to other contexts, such as online bullying.

Apple is planning to launch a news app this year, inviting publishers to participate. However, the terms of this invitation, which include allowing Apple to place ads next to their content and requiring publishers to indemnify Apple if legal issues arise, must be accepted unless explicitly opted out. Some publishers are concerned about this opt-out approach, claiming they shouldn't be bound by the terms without actively consenting to them. Legal experts suggest that the terms are industry standard, but the opt-out requirement might be difficult to enforce.

The article discusses the concerns and anxiety on the US territory of Guam due to North Korean threats, with local authorities downplaying any imminent danger while residents prepare for potential escalation. The island, home to important strategic US military bases and civilians, is seen as a possible target for Pyongyang if it decides to attack the US.

Sentinel-1b was launched into orbit by a Soyuz rocket from French Guiana as part of the European Union's flagship space project, Copernicus, which aims to monitor Earth's health and environment with a multitude of applications, including tracking shipping lanes for pollution and icebergs, and observing land surfaces for signs of subsidence. The satellite will work alongside Sentinel-1a, and the pair will map the entire Earth every six days. Simultaneously, Microscope, a French space agency mission, was also launched as part of the same flight, conducting a fundamental physics experiment investigating the equivalence principle, an aspect of general relativity, by precisely measuring the rate at which differently composed metal cylinders fall in the vacuum of space.

The article suggests that the pound has gained 1% due to the snap election call by Theresa May, which markets interpret as a potential win and larger majority, reducing her dependency on hardline Eurosceptics, and possibly leading to a softer Brexit. However, a larger majority could potentially lead to less focus on urgent priorities like negotiating the best EU deal and improving UK productivity, as indicated by some business groups. Economically, the window for this political gamble is open as the average wages are rising faster than prices, and there are a record number of people in work.

A hiker named Pavlina Pizova got lost during a hike on the Routeburn track in Fiordland National Park with her partner Ondrej Petr, who subsequently died after slipping on an icy slope. After leaving his body, Pizova spent the night out in the open, then broke into a hut where she stayed for nearly a month. When her concerned relatives posted on Facebook, a search was initiated, leading to Pizova's rescue. Petr's body has since been recovered, and a coroner's inquiry was launched.

Elena, a 40-year-old Muscovite, and her husband are struggling to manage their debt of over a million roubles due to banks, leaving them below the poverty line with only 10,000 roubles after sorting their cash. High levels of debt due to easy credits, decreased income, and insufficient regulations are causing financial difficulties for millions of Russians, including the possibility of losing one's only dwelling.

The Denver court has denied media requests for expanded coverage of the James Holmes case, the suspect in the Batman movie shooting that killed 12 and injured 58, while his first court appearance was filmed despite objections from his defense team. Holmes appeared dazed and was reportedly wearing a face guard due to spitting at prison officers. The shooting has spurred calls for gun control in Congress, but with elections approaching, there is no imminent action expected. Other developments include a visit from Batman star Christian Bale to the hospitalized victims, a baby boy born to a survivor whose husband remains critical, and increased security at cinemas following the shooting.

The Art Recovery Group, headed by Christopher Marinello, is working to combat the international art market trafficking of looted Syrian antiquities, by running the Art Claim database, checking international auction houses, online marketplaces, and aiding law enforcement in identifying and recovering stolen art. The group aims to stop the crisis by ending the conflict, increasing awareness among collectors, and maximizing resources dedicated to art crime units.

The report, following the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant disaster, highlights severe lapses in safety standards, emergency procedures, and a lack of governance by the plant operator, government, and regulators. The disaster was found to be a man-made disaster stemming from deep-seated Japanese cultural conventions such as obedience, groupism, and insularity. The accident wasresult of collusion, negligence, failure to develop safety requirements and evacuation plans, inadequate emergency response, and a lack of commitment to public health and safety the government and regulators.
